records.name: 1 0 1 FUN Bot
records.details:
These robots come in a variety of looks dependent on the entertainment, but most of them have human characteristics. While their components are quality, the humanoid versions show their age due to not looking realistic.

1 0 1 FUN Bots are often deployed in the Eldster blocks as amusement bots. With a variety of models, the bots function to entertain the masses. Unfortunately, their humour is dated to the year that the machines were produced so the humour or type of entertainment can be jarring. Eldster blocks are required to have a minimum of 1 robot per floor to keep inhabitants engaged and recognise "departures" so that much needed rooms may be filled with other crocks. Note the 1 0 1 FUN machines are built with quality components and are expected to still be in use when both their looks and jokes come back into fashion. Made by the Rumbelows company, these robots haven't been copied by any of the other robot producing companies.

records.name: A.R. Lab
records.sub: Sector 21 · Applied Robotics · Owner: Applied Robotics Trust · 249 floors
records.details:
The foremost leaders in applied technologies. Recently took a hit in the share market with their association with the Robot Wars and the awakening of Kenneth. However they are expected to bounce back.



Applied robotics deliver corporate level machinery rather than commercial small robotics. That said, the technology produced quickly finds its way into the commercial sector.



Rumors of a potential reactor meltdown within the building during the Robot Wars remain uncorroborated at this time.



One of the largest number of scientists in Sector 21.

records.name: Air-Scrubber Mini-Unit
records.details:
Utility / Home

A compact cube-shaped air purifier made from white plastic that yellows over time. The front features a slotted intake grille with dust permanently embedded in the corners. A small rotary fan inside spins behind a charcoal filter panel, visible through the slats. The top has a single toggle switch labeled "LOW / HIGH" in faded blue text.

The unit vibrates slightly when running, producing a rattling noise that grows louder as the filter clogs. The rear vent blows out air that smells faintly of charcoal and warm electronics.

PERFORMANCE
Removes roughly 40% of airborne particulates; struggles with smog surges. The filter must be rinsed weekly, and the casing cracks if dropped. Powered via a thin two-prong cable with frayed insulation.

HISTORICAL CONTEXT
Mass-produced during the Smog Surge of 2080, when air quality dropped below safe levels. As one civilian put it: "Breathing feels optional without one."

records.name: Alexa De Paris
records.details:
Glasses, often pink or purple hair, slight figure, green eyes

Paris is a very clever crook, she's often a mercenry, never kills but has yet t be cornered. Has done time for safe cracking, but rarely leaves clues. Her hiests are normally planned, We suspect her for several vault jobs but have little evidence to pin it to.

records.name: Alice Chambers
records.details: A sharp, bespectacled young woman with strawberry-blonde hair, dressed in a white lab coat over black office wear with a green staff ID badge clipped to her lapel.

records.name: Anna Kee
records.details: A sharp-eyed young Judge with strawberry-blonde hair, pistol raised and badge reading 'KEE' on her shoulder armour.

records.name: Antons Diner
records.details:
Anton's mascot is a throwback to a 20th-century dinosaur, a kitschy relic that somehow still draws in all sorts of visitors, most of them convinced this is the absolute epitome of style. There's no waitstaff to be found - service here is fully automated, gumball machines and all.



The diner itself is loosely themed on the classic 20th-century flick Back to the Future, though anyone who's actually seen the film would tell you it bears almost no resemblance. Its prized centerpiece is a battered body warmer, proudly displayed and treated as an utterly priceless article - supposedly once worn by the film's star, Michael J. Fox himself. It is, in fact, nothing of the sort.



During the Robot Wars, Anton's gumball machines briefly turned hostile and started attacking Judges, forcing a temporary closure while the Sector House got things back under control. Business has since resumed as normal.



Sitting close to SkyHigh Bank, Anton's pulls in a steady stream of high rollers looking for a slice of nostalgia - though it remains just as popular with the locals.

records.name: Arkham Asylum
records.sub: Sector 21 · Gotham City · Owner: Gotham City Government · 3 floors
records.details:
Very little is known for certain about Arkham Asylum. It sits within Gotham City itself, a location reachable only through a dimensional portal - instances of which have occasionally been sighted here in Mega City One. Access to these portals is strongly condemned by the Judicial Department; failing to report any sighting or use of one is itself a criminal offense.



The asylum is believed to hold superpowered beings under close guard, though details of exactly who and what is contained within remain sparse. The facility spans three floors, owned outright by the Gotham City government, and is said to house up to forty inmates alongside a staff of thirty guards and fifteen doctors.

records.name: Atlantis
records.details:
Atlantis is a mid-ocean station and underwater complex situated in the Black Atlantic, roughly halfway between Mega City One and Brit-Cit. Jointly patrolled by both mega-cities, it serves as a strategic outpost watching over the crossing - and, less officially, as a haven for expats and fugitives looking to disappear between jurisdictions.



With allegiance split between two allied but distinct powers, Atlantis has a long history of being the setting for political and military flashpoints whenever relations between Mega City One and Brit-Cit grow strained.

records.name: Automated Mini-Med Unit
records.details:
Top Secret - Sector 21 Deployment Only - Autonomous Medical Response Vehicle
Designation: AMMV-01 "Street Surgeon"

Forged from repurposed tank components and wrapped in reinforced armor plating, the Mini-Med is a compact miracle of battlefield engineering - three feet of unstoppable triage precision. Beneath its indestructible shell hums a high-efficiency battery core, driving a self-navigating chassis capable of threading through debris, alleys, and chaos at Judge-grade speeds.

When a medical emergency is flagged and the scene is clear of violence, the Mini-Med rolls out - silent, swift, and surgical. Its onboard AI scans vitals, dispenses aid, and stabilizes casualties before human med-teams arrive. But inside that armored shell lies delicate life-support tech - fragile, intricate, and easily compromised if struck.

If hostilities erupt, the Mini-Med disengages instantly, calling in Judges and vacating the zone. It's not built for confrontation - it's built for survival and salvation.

Sector 21 keeps its eyes low on these machines. "Eyes in the Sky" surveillance avoids them entirely - too much attention risks exposure. Outside the sector, they're rumor, myth, or classified ghost.

JUDGE OPERATIONS MEMO - SECTOR 21 (Eyes-Only / Level Omega)
Subject: Automated Mini-Med Vehicle (AMMV-01)

Sector 21 has begun limited deployment of the Automated Mini-Med Vehicle - a compact autonomous medical unit designed for rapid civilian triage. The AMMV-01 operates independently, responding only to verified emergency signals where violence is not present. It is not a combat asset.

Each unit is built from repurposed tank components, rendering the exterior virtually indestructible. However, the internal medical systems are delicate. Any damage sustained during aid delivery will compromise its function. If hostilities arise, the unit will immediately disengage and call for Judge intervention.

The Mini-Med is fast, efficient, and self-navigating. It will avoid confrontation and vacate any scene where aggression is detected. Units are currently restricted to Sector 21 only. "Eyes in the Sky" surveillance has been instructed to minimize observation to prevent public awareness.

Treat these machines as classified assets. Do not discuss their existence outside authorized channels.

DIRECTIVE
If you see a Mini-Med in motion, clear its path. It's saving lives under the radar.

records.name: Avery Chuckwaster
records.details:
Young, slick, male brown hair and grey eyes. Normally business attire (what is it with suits?). 6ft and slim and athletic.

Avery Chuckwaster is a slick businessman. Entering into partnership with Mahoney money bags in 2097 the duo acted as auditors for most of the mega city one big businesses. Something has changed in the last year has all shares have transferred to Mahoney moneybags. This could be some kind of a tax Dodge. No doubt a legal one, we have yet to pin anything on Mahoney moneybags. He's always careful and clean, a picture of the correct way to do everything, so much so the department use him as a specialist and consultant on forensic accounting crimes. Every chuckwaster had the same rap but not quite the same mind as Mahoney moneybags. His mental aptitude is standing, psi judges have rated him off the scale calling him computer like. He has no PSI ability however which seems to frustrate the PSI judges of sector 21 because we have no high-level psi operators. Chuck has had several jobs through make a city one always moving where the biggest paycheck was until his job security with Mahoney moneybags.

records.name: Back of Marleys Sugar Factory
records.sub: Sector 21 · Back of Marleys Sugar Factory · Owner: Whaler Incorporated
records.details:
Marleys is an old but still fully operational sugar factory, its automated robots and machinery grinding away at full capacity around the clock, seemingly indifferent to the world around them. An old tannoy system still crackles out mellow island rhythms over the factory floor - a faded holdover from whatever the place used to be, long since forgotten by most of the current workforce.



Recently, a local gang has quietly taken over the building. The sugar production continues uninterrupted, giving them a perfect legitimate front - crates go out the front door full of sugar, and whatever else goes out the back door tends to draw far less attention.

records.name: Bart Baz
records.details: A bright yellow, cartoonish young man with a spiky hairstyle, dressed head-to-toe in a matching yellow tracksuit, pictured against a neon cyberpunk cityscape.

records.name: Bart Hurman
records.details: Shares the same bright yellow cartoon character design as Bart Baz — spiky hair and a matching yellow tracksuit — but pictured against a plain background.

records.name: Bashar Tarr
records.details:
Dark Brown hair and brown eyes, stands 6'3ft. Bashar is curt but polite. Strong, muscular build, but agile.

Bashar Tarr is ex-Citi-Def. Having seen his talents first hand, Tess O'Sean employed Bashar to manage security for Razor Electronics. Tarr has changed many personnel seemingly due to poor quality or individuals susceptible to bribery. Bashar takes his role extremely seriously even when it comes to Judges' questioning. He is never offensive or not forthcoming with the truth but his loyalty is with the company. Tarr has foiled many attempts to steal merchandise and secrets from the Razor Electronics premises, always handing the offending citizens over to close by Judges. Bashar seems on the level. He doesn't believe in robots, but given that the company produces the warbot range he has several at his disposal. Bashar is clearly tactically astute and he's rarely surprised by anyone including Judges. Does this mean he has inside knowledge? Previous investigations have turned up nothing on Tarr as preparation seems to limit his need for violence.

records.name: Basil Rumbelow
records.details:
A distinguished elderly man with swept grey hair, glasses and a moustache, dressed in a sharp three-piece suit with coloured trim, cigar in mouth and walking with two canes.

Presumed to be the head of the Rumbelows company, manufacturer of consumer robotics including the 1 0 1 FUN Bot line.

records.name: Baxter Dipple
records.details:
Mousy brown hair and timid nature. Total geek

Dipple is a young programme tipped to be the next best thing. Sector 21 Tek Judges have been monitoring his progress. After being engaged with one of the biggest MC1 programming/computer agencies he worked on several high profile accounts. He seems to now be unemployeed however - possibility of self employment?

records.name: Baxter Hanger
records.sub: Sector 21 · Baxter · Owner: Richard Storm Holdings
records.details:
The Hanger is Baxter's dedicated vehicle shipping facility, where everything from freight haulers to personal runabouts is received, serviced, and dispatched onward across Mega City One and beyond. It's the noisiest part of the complex by a wide margin, with engines rarely falling silent for long.



Security here is tighter than the rest of the complex, given the sheer value of stock passing through on any given day.

records.name: Baxter Massive Warehouse
records.sub: Sector 21 · Baxter · Owner: Richard Storm Holdings
records.details:
The largest single structure in the Baxter complex, the Massive Warehouse handles the overflow the standard Warehouse can't fit - bulk freight, oversized containers, and anything else too big or too plentiful to store anywhere else in Sector 21.



Automated gantries and loader-bots handle most of the heavy lifting, with only a skeleton crew of human staff on-site at any given time to oversee operations.

records.name: Baxter Power Plant
records.sub: Sector 21 · Baxter · Owner: Richard Storm Holdings
records.details:
The Power Plant keeps the entire Baxter complex running, supplying every warehouse, the Hanger, and the Control Room with all the power they need to operate around the clock. It's a largely automated facility, with only a small technical crew required to keep watch over the reactors.



Judicial safety inspections here are more frequent than most, given how much of Sector 21's logistics network would grind to a halt if anything went badly wrong.

records.name: Baxter Warehouse
records.sub: Sector 21 · Baxter · Owner: Richard Storm Holdings
records.details:
Baxter Warehouse is the flagship storage facility for the wider Baxter logistics complex, owned outright by Richard Storm Holdings. Crates, containers, and pallets move through here around the clock, sorted and redirected onward to their next stop in Sector 21 or beyond.



The building itself has stood for decades, its original architecture long since swallowed up by extensions, cladding, and retrofits - though a few of the old-timers on staff still swear the original ground floor lobby had a very different name stencilled above the door.

records.name: Baxter Warehouse Control Room
records.sub: Sector 21 · Baxter · Owner: Richard Storm Holdings
records.details:
The nerve center of the entire Baxter operation, the Control Room coordinates shipments, staffing, and security across every other building in the complex. Wall-to-wall monitors track stock levels and vehicle movements in real time, giving whoever's on shift a god's-eye view of the whole operation.



An old, faded company portrait still hangs in the corner of the room - some long-forgotten founder posing proudly in front of a building that, if you squint, looks suspiciously unlike anything actually built in Sector 21. Nobody currently on staff seems to know or care who he was.

records.name: Bill Finger
records.details:
6 feet 2 inches, of fit, muscly, build. Brown hair and grey eyes, Finger is a strong dour individual with no distinctive characteristics other than his muscly physique.

Bill Finger is one of the wealthy elite in Sector 21. His wealth estimated in the billions, Bill Finger is a philanthropist with a good public image. Known for a huge range of inventions that are common place throughout MC1 from Shape Capes to Taser Gloves [on trial in Sector 1], lie detector [early model is the basis for the birdie] to ice skates, the diversity is vast. He has been called Mr Gadget by the press, however he does not use it in marketing. Finger's Parents were killed as a boy. His first invention the block-boomerang, that allowed you to throw a boomerang out of your block window and have it return through the same window, was the first mass produced of his equipment. This netting him his first million credits before the Judge Manis banned the device after citizens fell from their windows trying to catch the returning device. A full investigation cleared Finger and the Justice Department paid a further million credits in recompense for ceasing production. It was soon after this that Finger signed a deal with the Chief Judge Goodman giving first patent on any blueprint to the Justice Department. [FILE: Finger Asset Purchase Policy RESTRICTED - Goodman]

records.name: Billy-Bob Boblett
records.sub: Security Guard, Finger Enterprises Lobby · Age 34
records.details:
5 feet 10 inches, broad-shouldered and solidly built from years working the lobby floor. Sandy hair, kind brown eyes, wears the standard Finger Enterprises security uniform pressed and immaculate. Speaks with a noticeable, unmistakable drawl that marks him out instantly among the clipped Mega-City accents around him.

Badge reads 'Biolly Bob Boblett' - not a typo. His actual name is Billy-Bob Boblett, but when he transferred to the Finger Tower lobby posting, HR flagged that another Billy-Bob Boblett was already on the company roster and refused to issue a duplicate badge. The clerk on the other end of the intercom, only half-catching his drawled-out spelling, printed what she thought she heard. Nobody's ever bothered getting it fixed - his teammates on the security detail find it far too funny to let go, needling him about it as an extension of the same drawl that got him mis-heard in the first place. He takes it all in good humour.

Boblett was orphaned young and taken in personally by Bill Finger - one of the very few acts of open charity Finger allows to become public knowledge. He's been fiercely, unshakeably loyal to Finger ever since, the kind of loyalty that doesn't ask questions. Finger, for reasons known only to himself, has taken to calling him 'his Robin' - the nickname has stuck company-wide, even though nobody outside Finger's inner circle seems to know quite why.

Affable to a fault - genuinely tries to help anyone who comes through the lobby, whether that's directions, a lost badge, or talking someone down after a bad run-in with the Judges. Popular with the rest of the security detail despite (or maybe because of) being an easy target for ribbing.

records.name: Block Robot
records.details:
A hulking, blocky industrial robot finished in bright orange with a white cross logo stencilled across its chest and a pair of stubby antennae on its head-unit. Years of service around the block have left its plating covered in a patchwork of stickers and decals.

A common sight in the corridors and service areas of the block, the Block Robot handles routine maintenance and heavy-lifting work too menial or too dangerous for citizen staff. Sturdy but slow, and not built for confrontation.

records.name: Block-Cam MiniPod
records.details:
Surveillance / Civilian

A small black plastic dome camera with a fisheye lens protruding slightly from the front. The lens is prone to scratches, giving footage a hazy look. A motion sensor sits beneath the lens, indicated by a tiny green LED that flickers inconsistently.

The base is adhesive, though most citizens reinforce it with tape or screws. The internal storage is a cheap 12-hour loop chip that corrupts easily.

SPECIFICATIONS
Connectivity: Wi-Fi and short-range beam-link. A soft click sounds when motion is detected. Common failure modes: false positives, corrupted footage, adhesive failure.

HISTORICAL CONTEXT
Widely used during the Hallway Stalker Scare. As one civilian put it: "Trust no hallway."

records.name: Block-Com Wall Terminal
records.details:
Communication / Infrastructure

A wall-mounted communication slab found in hallways, stairwells, and communal landings. The housing is a rust-pitted steel box with chipped yellow paint and exposed screw heads. A flickering CRT sits behind a scratched plexi-shield, its corners darkened from years of burn-in. The keypad below is grimy, with half the numbers worn to smooth plastic; several keys click unevenly or stick.

A small speaker grille on the lower right emits a constant low hum, occasionally crackling with static. A faded sticker reads "PROPERTY OF CITYNET - DO NOT REMOVE," peeling at the edges. The terminal smells faintly of ozone and mildew.

INTERFACE
Voice-to-text input (rarely accurate), emergency broadcast override, block-wide announcements, and a "Call Judge" button (usually nonfunctional).

OPERATIONAL NOTES
Screen flickers during high-crime hours. Often vandalized with graffiti, stickers, or scorch marks. Sometimes used as a makeshift message board with taped notes.

HISTORICAL CONTEXT
Installed after the Broadcast Reform Act of 2081 mandated public access terminals. As one civilian put it: "If it doesn't shock you, it'll ignore you."

records.name: Bobby Jobby
records.details:
A lean, dark-blond young man usually seen in a battered brown leather-and-plaid jacket over a striped shirt and cargo pants — the picture of a rich kid dressed down to blend in on the street.

Bobby Jobbie is heir to the Sparkles Enterprises empire. Whilst not engaged in his father's business he seems to be spending a large portion of his father's money. His recent whereabouts have been questioned by the Sector Chief Deacon Stoll. It is not clear whether he is mixed in with the Tommy Gun Crime Syndicate, however his whereabouts have marked similarities to suspicious activities from the syndicate. Bobby does play an active part in his father's philanthropic duties, but is this to hide his criminal activities? On recent investigations of his father nothing was found. On secretive offshoot investigations of Bobby it was found that he is rarely accompanied by any security. This makes him very vulnerable, how long before this is realised by the criminal element of Sector 21. Bobby does not venture out of sector 21 it has been noticed.

records.name: Boing
records.details:
Controlled Substance - Recreational / Hazardous - Illegal for Civilian Use
Containment handled by Tek Division / Street Judges.

TECHNICAL OVERVIEW
A synthetic polymer gel, clear or pale blue and viscous in its raw form. Solidifies on contact with air, forming a flexible, transparent shell. Creates a personal anti-gravity field that lets the user bounce at extreme velocity. Effects last 30-60 minutes depending on dosage and exposure.

HAZARDS
Impact trauma is common - users often misjudge rebound trajectories. Boing shells resist small-arms fire and blunt impact, making containment difficult. Legally Class-A restricted; possession is punishable by up to 20 years in iso-cubes.

HISTORICAL CONTEXT
Developed by Recyc Corp in the late 2080s as a crowd-control polymer, then quickly repurposed by citizens for recreational "bounce-runs." Banned after the Sector 21 Boing Massacre of 2091, when 47 civilians collided mid-air during an illegal bounce-race.

records.name: BOING Pinball
records.details:
A cut-price cousin of the Pinboing Stadium, BOING Pinball franchises the same basic pitch on a smaller footprint: a human-scale pinball table where the "ball" is a citizen sprayed head-to-toe in Boing, a proprietary bounce-plastic that degrades naturally and harmlessly out of existence a few hours after application. Cheap, disposable, and - allegedly - safe. The franchise's lawyers have built an entire defence around that last word.



The machine is presently out of commission, undergoing repairs after Mister Black, a known blitzer, settled a dispute the old-fashioned way and put a rocket launcher through the playfield. Management is billing it as "scheduled maintenance."



The high score currently belongs to Bouncing Bob Bingley, a fact he treats with open contempt - he's since moved his talents exclusively to the big leagues at Pinboing Stadium and considers this branch beneath him. Two deaths have been recorded inside the machine over its operating history, both quietly filed as incidents "outside the boundaries of the franchise" - a distinction that satisfies the paperwork if nothing else. The Judges, for their part, mostly look the other way: whatever else Boing is doing, it's keeping a certain kind of citizen bouncing around inside a plastic bubble instead of causing the same trouble out on the street.

records.name: Brian Ritter
records.details:
Bald, no distinguishing features. Median build, average weight.

Brian has undergone 2 seperate Crime Blitzes, both uncovering little. An expert at electronics and computing, it is strange that he settles for being an accountant. While psych tests show no abilities, his mental aptitute is massive. PSI division have been frustrated at his natural mental block to their powers that he is able to hide behind. He's withstood 3 days interogation to break his resolve. Brian does nothing but his job. Records are clean, his movements are limited between his home and Rumbelows.

It's since come to light that Brian Ritter was living a full double life: under the fabricated identity "Gremmil Stiener," complete with an invented mother ("Charlotte Steiner") and a second full employment record, he also worked as an accountant at the Titan Mining Corporation - drawing two incomes while quietly enabling the illegal Obalmond procurement on both ends. Gold Team's fraud investigation uncovered the paper trail (see "Fraud of Brian Ritter (Double Identity)"); Green Team, working his death as "Gremmil Stiener" from the Titan Mining Corporation side, hadn't yet connected the two cases when Ritter/Stiener was killed by Turk Malloy to protect the procurement secret (see "Death of Gremmil Stiener" and this record's own murder case).

records.name: Bubble-Fizz Can
records.details:
Beverage / Civilian

A standard aluminum drink can with bright neon graphics and multiple pressure warnings printed in tiny text. The can is slightly heavier than normal due to the unstable foam formula inside. The pull-tab is reinforced with a thicker hinge to prevent accidental rupture.

When opened, the drink releases a violent burst of expanding foam that can overflow instantly if not handled carefully. The foam leaves sticky stains and carries a strong artificial fruit scent.

FLAVORS & HAZARDS
Cola-Burst, Citrus-Shock, and Berry-Boom varieties. Texture: fizzy, aggressively foamy. Hazards: clothing stains, minor chemical burns, explosive ruptures.

HISTORICAL CONTEXT
Banned in elevators after multiple foam-flood incidents. As one civilian put it: "Open it wrong and it becomes a weapon."

records.name: Call-Me-Kenneth
records.details:
Ex large carpenter robot. Bright red with three eye cameras. Large bipedal robot.

Normally descriptions detail the function of a robot, however CMK is arguably the leader of the first ever robot revolution. He has appeared on Tri-vid screens as part of a plan to rid the world of humans. While retaining his carpentry functionality it's clear the robot is smarter than planned. He appears angered and vengeful. He is armoured and seems to have a plan.

records.name: Cassandra Shoggles
records.details: <Redacted>

records.name: Chamber
records.details: A grim figure in a long, weathered trench coat with glowing red eyes, walking alone through a rain-slicked, neon-lit street at night.

records.name: Charles Bridger
records.details: <Redacted>

records.name: Charlton Heston Block
records.sub: Sector 21 · Charlton Heston Block · Owner: Pen Hestonettes · 1 floors
records.details:
Home to the highly illegal "Free the Guns" Society. The Heston Block is thought to be the block with the most fire power in Sector 21. How they're hiding guns is unknown, and where they're getting them from is unclear, even with PSI help, never the less, Heston Block is a dangerous place when it boils. 



Most inhabitants are a danger to themselves rather than others, as such Heston hasn't been raided. That together with the casualties that are likely means that it remains off limits for the time being.



The "We did not Evolve" group with the slogan "Take your stinking paws off me, you damned dirty ape!" Seems to be taking hold, pointing the finger at mutants, reports of mutants through the hotline is increasing exponentially. It's likely this is linked. Grafitti with the slogan is being seen more and more on buildings, thank goodness we don't have apes in society, what would happen then doesn't bear thinking about.

records.name: Cheesy McGee
records.details:
Brown hair and glasses. Short and skinny, he normally has a moustache. Big mouth and big reputation, he likes judges... Weird...

Cheesy McGee is well known throughout Sector 21 judges and is often seen clinging to the back of a speeding Lawmaster reporting on site. He's one of the few people allowed out of the Mega Corp Campus Building Cheesy belongs to MC1 News. He has worked his entire life as a reporter, and it is through this job that it is suspected that he holds a vast amount of knowledge over various judges, gangs, individual citizens, important elite members of Sector 21 and possibly MC1 in general. Cheesy has been described as an annoying itch you just can't scratch, being everywhere you don't want him to be at just the time you don't need him to be there. His investigative talent is second to none and this has seen him rise to the top of his peers. Cheesy is on primetime Tri-D programming. Everyone knows who he is both on TRI-D and important circles. Many have tried to get him on side, but he seems to be fair, if irritating. As such Judge Deacon Stoll grants him some special access to the Sector House in order to buy goodwill. Cheesy is involved in multiple investigations into crime. What they are, we do not know at any particular time however he has known to break stories to judges prior to the public in order to be at the bust. How much of his "right place at the right time" knowledge is due to bribery, corruption, blackmailing, or goodwill is unknown. Cheesy however is above reproach in Sector 21 at this time.

Cheesy McGee is deceased - killed in the infamous Vending Machine Shootout outside a notorious chop shop. Gold Team, in the middle of a wholesale slaughter of three vending machines during the raid, gunned Cheesy down in what everyone involved swore was a safe area, making him an unintended casualty of one of Sector 21's stranger firefights.

records.name: Chester Dibblethwait
records.details:
Rich elite, smart dressed, intelligent and cool when questioned. Usually accompanied by staff including security. Bald, 6ft tall and athletic with brown eyes.

One of the uber rich of MC1. Chester has been known to buy whole buildings to have them reduced to rubble for spoiling his view. This practice has been outlawed due to lack of housing for citizens. There's a certain amount of disconnection with the citizens of MC1 given his lofty status, but he's clean. Tek judges have tested his fortune and he seems an astute business man. He's had several assassination attempts carried out on him, all failing and not requiring Judge help, his security force is huge and very well trained… and paid. His most recent acquisition in the Sky High Bank.

records.name: Church
records.details:
"All Paths Lead Here."

Known simply as "The Church," this colossal cathedral-block dominates the skyline of Sector 21. It was designed as a utopian experiment: a single mega-structure where all faiths, philosophies, cults, and spiritual movements could coexist under one roof. The building is breathtaking - towering stained-steel arches, holo-scripture projectors, floating prayer platforms, incense-fogged atriums, and sanctuaries carved into every level, each floor housing a different belief system, from ancient Earth religions to bizarre Mega-City One micro-cults.



Coexistence, it turns out, is a fantasy. The Church is one of the most riot-prone structures in the entire sector, with faiths clashing constantly over space allocation, noise levels, ritual scheduling, donation rights, proselytizing zones, and who gets the "prime altar" during holy days. Visitors are welcomed warmly by some groups and aggressively criticised by others, and crossing from one faith's floor to another often sparks shouting matches, turf disputes, or full-scale theological brawls. Judges refer to The Church, without much affection, as "The Holy War Waiting Room."



Notable features include the Unity Spire, a massive central chamber meant to symbolize harmony and mostly used for protests; the Silent Floor, a neutral meditation zone enforced by stun-drones; the Donation Vault, guarded by Judge-approved accountants; and the Ritual Rotunda, a rotating platform that changes ownership hourly. The Church also carries an open grudge against Kelly's News, for selling gossip chips about clergy scandals.



The atmosphere is one of perpetual holy tension - The Church is almost always on the brink of a riot. Judges maintain a permanent presence on Floors 1, 20, 40, and 60, the sector's designated "flashpoint floors."

records.name: Commissioner Gordon
records.details: A grey-haired, moustached older man in glasses and a trench coat over a suit — the weary, dependable face of Gotham PD leadership.

records.name: Cornelius Stirk
records.sub: Thinks himself a Demi God · Age Unknown
records.details:
Male that looks old and frail with big beedy eyes, 5ft tall. Often appears manic. Can hide his appearance with PSI powers!

Extremely dangerous! Believes that eating people's hearts (the more  scared they are when he does it the better) gives him power. This does not seem the case however, his PSI powers are considerable without any foods.

records.name: Dallas Towers
records.sub: Sector 21 · Dallas Towers · Owner: J.R.Ewing · 234 floors
records.details:
Dallas Towers is currently under Judicial control via a mimic droid that Gold Team used to replace the incarcerated J.R. Ewing (previous owner). After faking his own death, J.R. is serving time in the cubes. After removing him from the building, it became clear that there were a number of measures he had taken to keep the building running.



A family feud between the Ewings and the Barnes makes this block volatile, not to mention its close proximity to Dynasty Block. Dallas Towers has an agreement to use solid fuel to power the building; this agreement has yet to be broken and holds up as law.

records.name: Deacon Stohl
records.details:
<Redacted>

Judge Deacon Stohl has a near perfect record for his many years on the street. Taking over from Judge Callaghan after the croc fiasco, stole was given command of sector 21. Style immediately arranged ring numeration and reparations for those affected by their miss placement and style has commanded sector 21 ever since. Stohl has a no-nonsense personality making him perfect for leadership roles. His 30 year duty roster on the streets of mega city one is exemplary with very few complaints. His arrest record is extremely high and crime invariably in the blocks he is assigned to is immediately reduced. Styles reputation precedes him self perpetuating this crime reduction wherever he travels. As style has got older in the sector his reputation when's, however his organisation and no-nonsense attitude still perpetuates rookies becoming good judges out on the street. His dislike of PSI judges is well known, for what reason he will not say, however he treats everyone fairly. Judge Stohl has taken down many crime rings in sector 21 and other sectors leading to many arrests including the chin brigade, the crime blitz syndicate, and the Mahoney family. For this reason he has many enemies however none of them are deemed able to penetrate the Sector House. Stohl is a respected Judge, cross him at your peril.

records.name: Demi Balendore
records.details:
Short bobbed black hair. Short, and slight, wears glasses. Grey eyes. business like attitude and seems cold when interacting. Smart in appearance and seems willing to please the tenants of the building she manages.

Demi Balendore has been employed by the El Supremo Plaza. Recent investigations into Balendore have been focused on the Plasa and its run down state and whether she was siphoning credits to her own accounts. This investigation is ongoing. Balendore has no convictions as yet and does not interact with any know perps. Deami lives in Michael Jackson Block, but has been known to reside at the Plaza on occasion. Having no parents of her own she seems committed to the occupants of the building.

records.name: Demolisher
records.details:
The Demolisher is a colossal, industrial-grade excavator designed for large-scale construction and earth-moving operations. Built for brute strength and endurance, it features reinforced treads, hydraulic arms capable of pulverizing concrete and rock, and a modular bucket system for leveling terrain.



Primary Function: Ground leveling, excavation, and relocation of massive earth volumes.



Design: Heavy armor plating protects its mechanical core and operators from debris and impact. The power system is a hybrid of hydraulic and plasma-assisted drives, giving it immense torque and stability.



Scale: Comparable to a small building in footprint, often deployed in megaprojects like city foundations, dam construction, or industrial reclamation zones.



Interior: Dual-operator cockpit with panoramic control panels, vibration dampeners, and autonomous stabilization systems.



Decline in Use: As urban expansion slows and fewer sites require major excavation, Demolishers have become rare relics of an era when cities still grew outward instead of upward. Many now sit idle in storage yards or are repurposed for demolition and salvage work.



Recently used for the rebuild of the S21 Megaways surrounding Rumbelows, near Pegasus Mechanix.

records.name: Dillon Wellopstein
records.details:
White mohawk and gormless. At 6ft 6, Dillon Wellopstein is a tall but scrawny guy.

Dillon Wellopstein is thought by the tech judges to be a patsy. While he is IT literate he does not have the brains to use the Neural-Spectre Link fully without detection. Nor is he able to create it, which he proclaims to. Wellopstein has a microscopic chip in his head that was a booby trap chip along the lines of professional blitzers however it was faulty, using faulty miniaturised explosives. However enough damage was done to Dillons brain that the PSI judges can't gain access to his brain. He seems to speak the truth but has little power over what comes out of his mouth other than being led through a conversation. He's currently doing time for his crime, but it is unclear whether he can be placed back in society once he's served his time.

records.name: Doctor Axon Optix
records.details:
Neuro adapters grafted onto the sides of his forehead. Genuis level intellect but a simple man. Often wears very dark optics due to his eye condition 5ft 8 and heavy set, greying hair.

Axon Optix was born with a genetic defect causing his retinas being weakened and susceptible to light. Teased throughout his life he's devoted his life to science. Initially his work revolved around his own condition, but it quickly moved to neural science. Now his inventions include the PSI-CHK, a machine that helps PSI-ops register latent PSI activity. Optix works in the esteemed William Osler Block where many other Doctors work on state of the art medical innovations. The Judicial Dept is monitoring his work as it has the potential to deliver a weapon against psychers for everyday street judges.

records.name: Door-Guard Alarm Pad
records.details:
Security / Low-Block

A thin adhesive sensor strip designed to stick to apartment doors. The casing is translucent plastic with a visible circuit trace running through it. A tiny red LED blinks intermittently, powered by a coin-cell battery housed in a small bump near the top.

A shrill speaker grille sits at the bottom, capable of emitting a piercing alarm when triggered. The adhesive backing is weak, often requiring tape reinforcement.

SPECIFICATIONS
Trigger mechanism: vibration and pressure detection. Battery life: 72 hours. Common failure modes: false alarms, adhesive failure, LED burnout.

HISTORICAL CONTEXT
Grew popular after the Sector 5 Break-In Wave, when burglaries spiked. As one civilian put it: "Keeps thieves out or drives neighbors insane."

records.name: Dwayne James
records.details:
A rotund man, largely due to his non stop Pepping practices. Dwane seems simple when you speak to him because he is. Rarely venturing out of his room, let alone Block, Dwayne is obese with mousy brown hair (normally under a Peeper's Bonnet and shades) and green eyes.

James Dwayne is employed by the judicial force as a peeper within the Dallas Towers building. Paid monthly, James reports back to Sector House 21 daily and M.A.C. refines the information along with other peepers in the sector. Dwayne was forced into peeping for the Sector House instead of going to the cubes for Voyeur offensives. He has paid minimal peeper allowances but has provided useful information on both Michael Jackson Block and Prince Block Citizens. He has yet to be wrong when reporting to Judges keeping detailed notes about all he sees. When dealing with Dwayne he should record what he sees as his memory is not evidence level quality according to PSI processing.

records.name: Dynasty Towers
records.sub: Sector 21 · Dynasty Towers · Owner: Croan Jollins · 232 floors
records.details:
Dynasty Towers is headed by Croan Jollyns. Much like J.R. in the local Dallas Towers, Croan keeps the building in check. Judges rarely need to enter the building - this may need to be re-visited, but while there is little trouble, they remain low priority.



Dynasty Towers contains both the Colby and Carrington clans. These families do not see eye to eye, but this has yet to escape the building into the streets or into other blocks. The building has wealth beyond many other buildings in MC1.



The Carringtons are expected to be in charge of the Cit-Def for the building - maybe this is why there is so little trouble.

records.name: Eddie Jam
records.details: A grinning, bald elderly man with a wild pink afro-wig, star-shaped sunglasses and a loud, clashing multicoloured tracksuit — dressed for a party, not a fight.

records.name: El Supremo Basement
records.sub: Sector 21 · El Supremo Plaza · Owner: Prince Melchiott (Dead) · 300 floors
records.details:
The El Supremo Plaza is Sector 21's biggest Crock Block, hosting a large proportion of the sector's senior residents. Many of the wrongly certified kook-cube residents of the "Big Kook-Up" [2190-2197] are housed here at the government's expense.



While the cost of staying in the Plaza is prohibitive to a mass of MC1 Sector 21, as a facility it is increasingly run down. An investigation is needed to determine the cause of this downturn. Cross Reference: Demi Balendore.

records.name: Finger Ent. Entrance
records.sub: Sector 21 · Finger Enterprises · Owner: Bill Finger · 253 floors
records.details:
Finger Enterprises house the 'Gadget Man's' home and business offices. The building is highly secure and has a vast array of robot manufacturing, keeping human employment to mere R&D. Employees at the site are trusted by the employer and have free access to the entire building.



While rich and a person of influence in the sector, Finger seems to be a law-abiding citizen, in as much as anyone is. Finger has become somewhat of a recluse over the last years - it's unclear if this is because of his age, or some vulnerability - but the "Gadget Man" still produces quality revolutionary products.



Finger's light touch on investigations may in some part be down to his offering of new products to the Judicial system first, before mass manufacturing for the MC1 citizens. Finger Enterprises has a division for weaponry that is closely followed by the judicial system - again, the Judge Council has first option on hardware.

records.name: Fork

Pink mohawk and minimal clothes. Acompanied by mirrorlike idiots

Spoon, fork, and whisk are triplets from a disturbed marriage between two disturbed individuals. The triplets quickly fell in with the wrong crowd and have been cubed more times than they've had birthdays. To say they are stupid is an understatement, Dredd thinks they share an IQ between them. And the one that has it, is never the one he meets at any given time. Most of their crimes have been simple robbery or taps. Over the past few months/year they have not been in the cubes, judge Cullis as an open question with the Street judges of Sector 21 as to whether they have been killed either  by their own stupidity or by some other gang. Always supporting the same haircut and very few clothes, The pink Pukes as they like to be called are easily recognisable. Report to Cullis any sightings.

records.name: G.F. Outside Markets
records.details:
G.F. Outside Markets is exactly what it sounds like: an open-air stall market, one floor, ten to twenty vendors on any given week, opening on a weekly cycle that draws all manner of traders happy to set up shop without asking too many questions of their neighbours. The permit belongs to Gill Bates, who by all appearances runs a scrupulously legitimate operation and remains, as far as anyone can tell, entirely oblivious to what else moves through his market.



What else moves through it is black-market tech - sold in small quantities, deliberately fragmented across enough stalls and enough weeks that no single transaction adds up to anything worth a warrant. Nobody closes a real deal on-site. Interested parties make contact, feel each other out, and take the actual business elsewhere, off the books and off the grid. The Judges have the market under standing surveillance and have yet to crack the system from the inside.



Sightings of Pendal, a name that keeps surfacing in connection with the market's deeper end of the trade, have been minimal of late. The "G.F." in the market's name invites an obvious assumption - that it's somehow tied to the Glimmerfish lawyers - which the market is quick to deny and which appears, on the available evidence, to be nothing more than the two of them sharing a postcode.

records.name: Glimmerfish Offices
records.sub: Sector 21 · Glimmerfish Offices · Owner: Mary Glimmerfish · 2 floors
records.details:
"Precision Is Power."

The Glimmerfish Offices occupy two pristine floors in the upper tier of Sector 19's Legal Spire, a rare pocket of order amid the chaos of Mega-City One. The building's glass facade gleams like a blade, reflecting the smog-choked skyline. Inside, everything is immaculate - polished chrome desks, holographic case files suspended mid-air, and silent drones that record every word for legal archives.



The atmosphere is tense and disciplined. Staff speak in hushed tones, aware that Glimmerfish herself is known to appear without warning, her presence enough to silence entire rooms. Her motto, "Precision Is Power," is etched above the entrance in cold blue light.



The firm's primary operations cover high-profile defense cases, corporate litigation, and Justice Department contract law. It maintains ongoing hostility with the MC1 News Network, for repeatedly leaking confidential case details, and with the Skull-Hammer Heights Legal Syndicate, a rival firm specialising in altogether more violent contract enforcement.

records.name: Gorgeous George
records.details:
Now becoming known for his theatrics, Gorgeous George wears a top hat and a fluorescent skull mask. Huge in stature, muscly, black hair and green eyes.

Gorgeous George has been in iso-cubes more than he's been out of them. A thug from an early age he never really amounted to anything else. He does however seem to have taken it to a new level. In his acts of brutality he is now known to wear a luminescent skull like a mask with a top hat! It is thought he is trying to make a brand of his violence. (Can this be considered a crime?) Rarely does gorgeous George hide from judges, again his combative nature with the judges sometimes resulting in his escape may be all part of his branding image. (We really should list a new crime around this phenomenon.) Gorgeous Georges acts of violence are limited to whoever has been targeted by the Tommy Gun crime syndicate, or whoever has annoyed him from one minute to the next. He seems to take great pleasure in hurting people no matter who they are. Clearly he is now muscle for hire, (Have the Tommy gun crime syndicate got him on a retainer?).

records.name: Gotham City
records.details:
Gotham City is a dark, Gothic-tinged metropolis gripped by rampant crime. Costumed vigilantes have taken it upon themselves to fight back against the corruption, operating alongside - and often instead of - a police force widely regarded as outdated and inept.



Gotham exists within a much larger world that has only recently become accessible to Mega City One, via a network of dimensional portals. Access to these portals is completely restricted, and failing to report any sighting or use of one is a criminal offense in its own right. A number of mutants and criminals have already been observed crossing over from the other side.

records.name: Grand Prix Block
records.details:
"The Apex of Velocity."

The Grand Prix Block is the crown jewel of Mega-City One's racing culture - a towering monument to precision engineering and ruthless competition. Built as the corporate successor to Nascar Block, it's cleaner, faster, and infinitely more dangerous.



The block's central feature is the Apex Circuit, a multi-tiered racetrack that spirals through the building's interior and exterior, merging real-space and holo-projection lanes. Races here are broadcast city-wide, with sponsorships worth millions and fatalities considered part of the spectacle.



Only licensed racers and their pit crews live inside the block. Apartments double as garages, and every resident is required to maintain a functioning vehicle. The block's motto - "The Apex of Velocity" - glows in gold neon across its upper decks. It runs on dual plasma-fusion cores and hits 160 dB during races. Judges maintain a permanent presence here, not to stop races, but to ensure the chaos doesn't spill into neighboring sectors.



Grand Prix Block carries an open rivalry with Nascar Block over racing supremacy, a grudge with the Municipal Building for refusing to pay emissions fines, and a feud with Kelly's News for leaking race-fixing scandals.



Grand Prix Block is a symphony of speed and danger. Every race is a high-stakes event, every crash a media sensation. The residents live for the roar of engines and the flash of victory lights.

records.name: Green Pieces
records.sub: Sector 21 · Green Pieces · Owner: Communittee Ownership · 156 floors
records.details:
Meaning so many things to so many people, this block is obsessed with saving the planet, one molecule at a time. Not even getting the name right, the place means well, but they often end up serving time in the cubes. 3 full-time Wally Squad members try to corral the locals, keeping them in check.



It's widely held that the basis for the building is a tree - however this is not the case, it's plasti-cement, shaped and painted when the Chief Judge ordered the building created to house the "greenies." Care should be taken not to start riots with the wasting of natural resources.

records.name: Gremmil Stiener
records.details:
Average Build, height and weight. Often bald or short back and sides blonde hair. No distinguishing features.

Gremmil Stiener is an accountant for the Titan Mining Corporation. The Titan Mining Corporation is under judicial law and as such is beyond reproach. Full screening of Gremmil was carried out before employment and monthly examinations via both psych and house visits are carried out on all staff. Gremmil is believed a model citizen and has no criminal ties to him or his family. He is an amateur Aeroball player and has several hobbies. None of these hobbies are considered illegal. Gremmil has always attended work on time and has yet to miss a day since being employed. Most of his family is deceased however his mother is at El Supremo Plaza a renowned Croc Block. Gremmil's education was exemplary, lucking into a sponsored school grant much to his mother's amazement. This has been investigated thoroughly with no leads. Gremmil leads a quiet life mixing only for his hobbies and work. He has been offered promotions in his job however his psych evaluation was correct in evaluating that he had no aspirations of furthering his career.

It's since come to light that "Gremmil Stiener" never existed as a separate person - the identity, family history ("Charlotte Steiner") and employment record were all fabricated by Brian Ritter, Rumbelows' own procurement accountant, to draw a second income while covering the illegal Obalmond shipments from both sides of the ledger. Ritter/Stiener was killed by Turk Malloy to protect the procurement secret - see "Death of Gremmil Stiener," "Fraud of Brian Ritter (Double Identity)," and the Brian Ritter case file.

records.name: Gutterman Ghett Block
records.sub: Sector 21 · Gutterman Ghett Block · Owner: Deceased Gutterman Ghett · 95 floors
records.details:
"Order Through Violence!"

Gutterman Ghett Block prides itself on being "civilized chaos." Its residents claim to be organized maniacs - they run their own militia, maintain a functioning black-market economy, and even hold weekly "civic assemblies" that usually end in fistfights. The block's architecture is brutalist and angular, with reinforced balconies and propaganda screens flashing slogans like "Order Through Violence!" and "Clean Streets, Dirty Souls."



The Ghett's self-appointed "Block Council" enforces its own laws, often clashing with Judges who consider the place a semi-autonomous war zone.

records.name: Halcon Jefferson
records.details: Newer addition to Blue Team - added alongside the existing roster (Byre, Edmund, Mercer, Shoggles, Skar), not a replacement for any of them.

records.name: HAMMU-00
records.details:
Omega-Black / Top Secret - Heavy-Class Autonomous Medical Response Vehicle
Designation: HAMMU-00 - unofficially "The Rolling Ward"
Location: Secured Storage - Sector 20 Mechanics Plant
Status: Prototype - Single Unit in Existence

Following the operational success of the compact Automated Mini-Med Units in Sector 21, R&D quietly constructed a heavy-class variant. This machine is not a scaled-up version - it is a mobile medical facility built on a repurposed armored transport chassis, standing over twice the height of a Judge and weighing enough to crack pavement on arrival. Its exterior plating is salvaged from decommissioned riot tanks, making it effectively immune to small-arms fire, explosives, and environmental hazards.

Inside, however, lies a labyrinth of delicate medical systems: trauma bays, automated surgical arms, chemical stabilizers, cryo-pods, and a high-capacity med-supply vault capable of supporting multiple city blocks during mass-casualty events. The internal tech is fragile - a single breach could compromise the entire unit.

HAMMU-00 is designed for:
- Mass-casualty response
- Inter-city medical transport
- Emergency supply relay during infrastructure collapse
- Rapid deployment to disaster zones

It is autonomous, but slow to maneuver in tight urban spaces. It will avoid confrontation at all costs. If violence is detected, it will immediately halt, seal its internal bays, and request Judge escort.

Only one exists. Only Sector 20 and 21 Command are aware of its presence. It is currently stored in the Sector 20 Mechanics Plant under full blackout protocols. "Eyes in the Sky" surveillance has been instructed not to track or highlight the unit - any aerial attention risks exposing the prototype to hostile actors or curious citizens.

DIRECTIVE
If HAMMU-00 is deployed, clear the streets. It's not just a vehicle - it's a lifeline on treads.

records.name: Harry Jobby

A greying, sharp-featured man who favours a high-collared tactical-cut coat with glowing trim over a camo undersuit — sharp enough to look every inch the self-made Sector 21 magnate, tough enough to look like he still gets his hands dirty.

Harry Jobbie, on investigation, is a happy go lucky rich guy. After tech judges forensically audited Sparkle Enterprises very little was turned up, resulting in multiple payments to Sparkle for damages. Harry is renowned for his philanthropic activities as well as his business enterprises. A self-made man, making fantastical kneepads for the rich. Harry is one of Sector 21's elite. Harry is a designer and still designs one-of-a-kind knee pads that are distributed through his subsidiary company Lotus Blossom. Harry's company Sparkle Enterprises is located in Sector 21 it has minimal security (this should be looked at) at each of his stores and central company location. Harry for the near future is above suspicion, as is his wife. Harry's son Bobby may need investigation, whilst nothing is reported RE criminal activity, is locations over recent months have included less than favourable areas. Possible stake out?

records.name: Heavy Metal Kid
records.details:
20 meters tall with facial features. Bipedal, but slow, the Heavy Metal Kids quickly look battered and beaten due to their usage.

A new design first revealed to the world at the Robot of the Year show, the Heavy Metal Kids are the top end in demolition robots. Each stands over twenty feet tall, and has two arms ending in vicious cutting claws with a third bearing a wrecking ball. As demolition robots, the Heavy Metal Kids relish all forms of destruction. Note that the Heavy Metal Kids are not a design of Rumbelows, but due to manufacturing constraints and their size, the plans have been distributed to the company via another vendor for the production of 5 in the sector.



The Heavy Metal Kid robots are programmed for major destruction within the city confines. Giant robots, they stand 20m tall with human characteristics of a child. Their ability to reason is minor, sticking to planned demolition tasks. Cited around the city there are not many Heavy Metal Kid mechs. The robots are designed specifically for destruction and demolition, and as such do not need any tools as these are integrated into their bodies. A majority of their requirement is brute force destruction of buildings/municipal facilities. The Heavy Metal Kids have a pacification mode that can be engaged by any judge within the city. Often controlled by overseer droids, the Heavy Metal Kids have primitive brain power. Often pitted one against another to improve workflow, the Kids are most childlike in their behaviour and must be watched at all times, although they are considered safe.

records.name: Hee Hee Spa
records.sub: Sector 21 · MICHAEL JACKSON BLOCK · Owner: JERMAIN TITO · 139 floors
records.details:
Block has an effigy of Michael Jackson  on the exterior. All interior dedicated to the deceased “King of Pop”. Something that you are reminded of every second you are in the building, whether it be the music that is constantly played on every floor even through the night, or the shops and services which are heavily linked even if only by name to the ex-singers work. 



The number five has specific interest to all members of the building. 



Floor five has an auditorium for concerts, used by Michael Jackson wannabes. 



Given the extremes that the tenants go to, most citizens avoid this block. Even the Citi-Def For the block call themselves The 'Bad' Boys. 



Note that Halloween is a particular problem time for the building given the Thrilla reference. Many citizens are literally scared to death on the day/night of the holiday regardless of many attempts to stop the event.

records.name: Hover-Disc Spinner
records.details:
Toy / Recreational

A lightweight polymer ring with a micro-thruster core embedded in the center. The outer rim features LED trail lights that flicker erratically. The underside has three tiny stabilizer vents that hiss softly when active.

When activated, the disc lifts a few centimeters off the ground and begins spinning rapidly. Its flight path is unpredictable, often veering toward walls or ceilings.

SPECIFICATIONS
Modes: Spin, Hover, and Chase. Battery: 20-minute charge via a flimsy USB-jack. Typical wear: scuff marks, cracked rims, burnt thruster vents.

HISTORICAL CONTEXT
Banned in schools after repeated ceiling damage. As one civilian put it: "Fun until it escapes."

records.name: Howdee Doodee NightClub
records.details:
Sitting one floor deep in the Will Shatner Block, the Howdee Doodee NightClub trades on a marionette from an ancient kids' show nobody currently drinking there has ever seen, and probably wouldn't recognise their own venue's mascot in a line-up. Management insists this is a feature, not a gap in the historical record.



The club runs a rotating slate of theme nights, but Star Trek Night is the one that actually pays the rent. Punters turn up in cheap poly-blend uniforms, argue over who called dibs on being the Captain, and spend the evening re-enacting whole episodes with a fidelity that would be almost impressive if half of them weren't three drinks past remembering their own lines. The Judges have long since stopped responding to "away team disputes" as anything other than standard drunk and disorderly.



Upstairs, the pole dancers work the room. Outside, business of a different kind - the "TJ Hookers," a loose outfit of call girls who've made the block's name their own personal branding exercise, working the pavement in the club's shadow.

records.name: Ico Belenchek
records.details:
The original mobster, heavy in the gold chains. Bald, green eyes and medium build, always in a suit.

Belenchek is often seen with petty criminal but never doing business with them. There's little to pin him to anything at the moment but he does seem to have his hands in many pies. Wally squad wants him turned as he's a suspected member of the Tommy Gun Crime Syndicate. Withough something good to pin on him it's not been worth pulling him off the streets. If you do get an opportunity, watch out for his minions, if we're turning him it'll need to be a good story so he's not shredded by his own people when we put him back in place.

records.name: Isabella Balton
records.sub: Temporal Physicist / CEO of Balton Industries
records.details:
An elderly woman with grey hair and glasses, in a white lab coat over teal medical scrubs — deceptively unassuming for someone rewriting the rules of causality itself.

Known as "The Architect of Time," Isabella Balton stands at the bleeding edge of science in the fractured reality of Mega-City One, a pioneer in temporal and spatial displacement who bends the laws of physics as easily as others bend the law itself. Her work blurs the line between genius and heresy, and the Justice Department watches her closely, unsure whether to fund her research or erase her from existence.

Balton leads the Chrono-Dynamics Division of Balton Industries, a corporate lab hidden deep within the ruins of Old Sector 12. Her experiments have opened rifts in time, controlled fractures that allow matter, memory, and even people to slip between moments. She began as a Judge-approved physicist working on temporal containment fields, technology meant to freeze crime scenes for forensic analysis, but her obsession with causality led her to push beyond sanctioned limits. When her experiments began producing temporal echoes (duplicates of people and events), the Department shut her down. She went underground, continuing her work under Balton Industries, officially a "materials research firm," unofficially a hub for time-fracture experimentation.

Isabella is brilliant, detached, and eerily calm. She speaks as if she's already lived the conversation before. Her mind operates in nonlinear loops: she remembers futures that haven't happened yet and forgets pasts that never were. Her demeanour unnerves even Judges; she's polite, precise, and utterly fearless. She views time not as a river but as a weapon, something to be shaped, redirected, and, if necessary, detonated.

Among scientists: "She's rewriting physics one paradox at a time." Among Judges: "A threat to causality itself." Among citizens: "The woman who can make yesterday disappear." Rumours claim Isabella has created temporal sanctuaries, hidden pockets of time where fugitives can exist outside the Judges' jurisdiction. Others say she's seen the end of Mega-City One and is quietly preparing for it.

records.name: J.R. Ewing
records.details:
JR always seems to be smiling, even when he's not supposed to be (as recent interrogation shows. A tall man with greying hair and increasingly heavy set. He oozes wealth and confidence. Always seen in a Stetson (the block's trademark attire) he has no other distinguishing features, however everyone in Dallas and Dynasty Blocks knows him

JR Ewing was arrested for wasting judges time and obstructing the law. Recently Gold Team investigated his Murder only to find that it was faked. This was to out his brother who he believed, correctly, Was trying to dispose of him. JR Runs the Dallas towers block very well it seems keeping even it's Barnes versus Ewings rivalry to a minimum. He has also set up a number of proprietary locking mechanisms and computer interfaces that are not judge identifiable. This alone would have sent him to the isocubes. Was the manner in which he kept The block quiet may not have been the best, it is undoubtable one of the quietist and trouble free blocks in sector 21. ++Gold Team Reference File RE installing JR back in Dallas Towers ++ JR upholds the trade/power coal rights For the building. Dallas towers is the only building in mega city allowed to use dirty fuel (carbon based). JR has a network of spies, fixes, security, techs, and influencers that help him run the building so efficiently. This may be a further investigation in regards to running other blocks that we have had troubles with. He is rich, and with a larger than life personality he seems divorced from the real lives of MC1 citizens.

records.name: Jordel Font
records.sub: Senior Investigator, Internal Conduct Division (Special Judicial Squad), Sector 21 - specializes in rooting out Judges who show signs of empathy, hesitation, or "street contamination"
records.details:
Judge Jordel Font serves in the Special Judicial Squad (SJS) - the Justice Department's internal affairs division, feared even among Judges. Where most Judges enforce the Law on the streets, Font enforces it within the ranks: he doesn't investigate corruption, he excises it. Identified early at the Academy of Law for his cold intellect and emotional detachment, he graduated top of his class in Judicial Ethics and Interrogation Procedures and was transferred straight to the SJS. He began his career as a compliance auditor reviewing case files for procedural irregularities, and his gift for spotting falsified reports led to the exposure of three rogue Judges and the execution of one.

Methodical, emotionless, and unnervingly polite - the kind of Judge who thanks you before ending your career. Font believes corruption begins with compassion and treats mercy as a virus; his speech is clipped, his tone surgical, his stare unblinking. Known catchphrase: "The Law does not forgive. It corrects."

Reputation precedes him on all sides. Among street Judges: "If Font asks for your case files, you're already guilty." Among the SJS: "Reliable. Efficient. Unsentimental." Among citizens: "The man who judges the Judges."

Tall and lean, kitted in black SJS armour with a matte finish and gold trim muted to near gray. His badge reads FONT, and his helmet visor reflects nothing. A compact data-scanner and a neural interrogation probe hang from his belt - his presence feels like a verdict waiting to happen.

records.name: Joseph Dredd
records.sub: Resigned Judge, now working undercover as a common laborer on the S21 megaway road crew
records.details:
A veteran Judge of Sector 21, known for a hard, uncompromising record even by Judges' standards. Resigned from active duty after unsuccessfully petitioning the Council to shut down all AI computers and robots during the Robot War - a position that put him at odds with the rest of the department.

The resignation was widely taken at face value at the time - a Judge who'd lost an argument with the Council walking away from the badge. It's since come to light that this was deliberate cover: Dredd used the road crew posting to get close to a string of explosions along the S21 megaways that seemed to be following a pattern nobody else had connected. With his help, casualties from the ongoing blasts have been kept to an absolute minimum (see the "Destruction of S21 Megaways surrounding Rumbelows" case file).

The pattern he tracked eventually pointed to J.C.N.2001's plan to isolate the Pegasus manufacturing plant hidden beneath Rumbelows. Dredd is not considered a suspect in the destruction - only a witness and asset who stayed embedded long after most would have blown their cover.

Also personally tied the string of S21 megaway explosions near Rumbelows to the earlier theft of the MC1 RoboMole tunneler - see "Broken Skedways" - and ran a joint undercover operation with the Shelley mimic droid trying to locate the hidden Pegasus manufacturing plant (see "Shelley Droid Sacrifice - Pegasus Infiltration").

records.name: Juan
records.details: A dapper, mustachioed man in a flamboyant red-and-orange ruffled tuxedo with black lapels and a red sash. Rarely seen without a bottle in hand, pouring drinks with a sly, knowing grin.

records.name: Judge Helmet
records.details:
Standard Issue - Protective Equipment - Active Service (All Divisions) - Street, Tek, Med, and Psi Judges
Manufactured by the Justice Department Armory, Sector 12.

TECHNICAL OVERVIEW
A full-coverage combat helmet built from a reinforced poly-ceramic composite with an internal shock-gel lining. Weighs 1.8 kg. The red polarized visor has adaptive tint and a HUD overlay. Comms include encrypted short-range radio, telemetry uplink, and a voice command interface, all run off a micro-cell battery good for 72 hours of operation. DNA-encoded for security - removal by unauthorized personnel triggers a stun pulse.

OPERATIONAL NOTES
The HUD handles target tracking, Lawgiver ammo readout, environmental scan, and M.A.C. access. Voice commands include "Record," "Transmit," "Zoom," and "Night-Vision." Tek Division recalibrates the optics weekly. Early Mk I visors are known to glare under neon light - corrected in the Mk II prototypes.

HISTORICAL CONTEXT
Introduced in 2086 alongside the Lawgiver Mk I. A symbol of authority and anonymity - the helmet conceals identity, ensuring judgment without bias.

records.name: Justice Monument
records.sub: Sector 21 · Justice Monument · Owner: Sector 21 Civic Order Division · N/A (210m statue) floors
records.details:
The Justice Monument is a colossal statue of a Judge standing sentinel over Sector 21, carved from reinforced ferro-stone and plated with blackened steel. The figure's visor glows faintly red at night, scanning the streets below like an eternal overseer.



Commissioned after the Sector 21 Riots of 2128, the monument was meant to symbolize unity and deterrence - but most citizens see it as a reminder that justice in Mega-City One never sleeps, never forgives, and never forgets. The Judge's pose is iconic: one hand gripping a Lawgiver pistol, the other resting on the Book of Sentencing, its pages etched with the words "Obey and Endure." Beneath the statue's feet lies a plaza known as Judgment Square, where protests, ceremonies, and executions have all taken place.



The monument stands 210 meters tall on a ferro-stone core with steel plating and servo-reinforced joints, maintained by the Sector 21 Civic Order Division, lit at night by red-white floodlights beneath its ever-active scanning visor. The Church holds an open grievance against it, calling the monument "idolatry of authority."



The statue itself is calm - silent authority - but the plaza below often erupts in tension. Citizens gather to protest, pray, or simply stare back at the Judge who never blinks.

records.name: Karl Rossum
records.details:
A short (5ft 3 inches tall) man with mousey brown hair, he is loud but sociable and often dresses in a suit. He has a scar on the back of his neck, a result of trying to escape Judge Manis.

Karl Rossum is an inventor of genius proportions. In 2088 Rossum was arrested for extortion. Further investigation showed Rossum was forced into the extortion. Bill Fingerhad been following the inventor before his run in with the law. He later hired Rossum after a stint in the cubes. Cube time was reduced for Rossum based on Finger vouching for the man. Finger later hired Rossum as a research assistant for his gadget company. The two later created HARDAC, a computer capable of controlling the entire building of Finger Enterprises. Rossum Has kept his nose clean since then. However he has been seen hanging around in the less opulent areas of the sector. As yet it is unknown why Rossum has been visiting these sectors, and an investigation is ongoing with Wally Squad. This investigation is set for three months, should it not find anything in that time Wally Squad members will be reassigned. Karl Rossum's inventions are well known in megacity 1, produced by Finger Enterprises.

Tall, slender and athletic. Melody is very charsmatic

Kasey Melody has been working at the Rise Up Garage for 1 year. She was on the books but barely. She is the only member of the Rise Up Garage other than Paersy House. Melody is a smooth operator, she's charming and can keep you talking.

records.name: Kelly's News
records.sub: Sector 21 · Kelly's News · Owner: Kelly · 1 + mezzanine storage loft floors
records.details:
"If it's happening, I've got it."

Kelly's News is a compact, high-tech news kiosk wedged between two towering mega-blocks in Sector 21. It's one of the few remaining independent news agents in Mega-City One - a relic of old-world commerce wrapped in neon, holo-screens, and reinforced plexi-glass.



The storefront is plastered with flickering headlines, rotating vid-feeds, and scrolling ticker bars that scream breaking news, riot alerts, and Judge bulletins. Inside, shelves are stacked with synth-paper tabloids, encrypted data-slates, gossip chips, and black-market "uncensored" news cubes. Stock runs the full spread: MC1NN official news slates, gossip chips and celebrity meltdown feeds, riot-zone bulletins, Judge-approved educational holos, and, sold quietly under the counter, suspected illegal "Free Vox" pirate broadcasts.



Kelly herself is a sharp-eyed, fast-talking proprietor who somehow keeps the shop running despite constant drone inspections and the occasional block-war spillover. Her motto, "If it's happening, I've got it," glows in blue neon above the counter. The shop maintains an open grudge with the Glimmerfish Offices, after Kelly leaked a high-profile case file to a rival outlet.



The atmosphere never settles - always busy, always loud, one customer away from a shouting match. Kelly keeps order the old-fashioned way, with a stun-baton kept within reach under the counter.
