records.details:
Slightly overweight and jovial, with excellent credentials as a chief. Landem is quiet but pleasant.

Unknown juve history, assumed lawful otherwise there would be more records. Pickle has worked at the El Supremo Plaza for a year moving from 'Beat It' egg restaurant in Michael Jackson Block. He's never been under investigation. He lives where he works creating delicacies for the crocks in the Plaza. Records state that he mingles with the guests of the block and is popular in the building.

Recently confirmed to be one of at least two aliases used by Micka Pendell, the genius programmer/engineer who vanished from tracking after leaving the Kook-Cubes years ago - the quiet, jovial chef persona at El Supremo Plaza was cover while Micka (also operating as "Mika Pendell") worked with J.C.N.2001 to build the Neural-Spectre Link (see the "Neural-Spectre Link" case file).

records.name: Lando Risk
records.sub: Civilian Scientist - R&D Tier-Red (Monitored) - inventor of the Plasti-Skin Coat · Age 37
records.details:
Lando Risk is a Sector-Class Innovator turned high-risk asset - a prodigy who struck gold before he was old enough to rent a lab without a co-sign. His breakthrough, the Plasti-Skin Coat, was hailed as a medical revolution: a self-grafting synthetic dermal layer that hardened on contact, protecting wounds until new skin formed beneath. Hospitals loved it. Trauma wards worshipped it. Then the gangs got hold of it - they tore through the factory, stole vats of the compound, and turned it into street-grade armor plating. Judges banned the substance within a week, but not before Risk had already sold the patent to William Osler Block for a fortune. Overnight, he became a wealthy man with a tarnished legacy - a genius whose invention saved lives but armed criminals.

Since the Plasti-Skin ban, Risk has kept his head down and his labs locked tight. Recently, something changed - he has poured vast sums into a new project, a top-secret experiment whispered about in R&D circles and flagged quietly by Sector Intelligence. Whatever he is building, it is big enough to make or break him.

He has been seen less in public, more in secured facilities. Supply shipments to his private lab have tripled. Energy consumption spikes at odd hours. The few technicians who have worked near him say he is running on caffeine, obsession, and the kind of desperation that only comes when a man is betting everything on one last miracle.

Risk is not reckless - but he is driven, brilliant, unpredictable. If this new project succeeds, it could rewrite his legacy. If it fails, it might bury him.

Rumor in the Blocks: "Risk made his fortune on skin. Now he is trying to build something tough on the outside and healing inside again, but on a bigger scale."

records.name: Large Carpark
records.details:
A standard multi-level Sector 21 carpark, stacked high enough to swallow whatever traffic the surrounding blocks throw at it. Rows of vehicles sit under flickering strip-lighting and a permanent haze of exhaust that the extraction fans never quite keep up with. Automated ticketing drones patrol the levels, more interested in booking violations than in anything resembling security.



Like every large carpark in the sector, it's less a destination than a symptom - a place people pass through, argue in, occasionally get mugged in, and otherwise forget the moment they've found the stairwell out.

records.name: Lawgiver Mk I
records.details:
Restricted - Judge-Issue Only - Standard Sidearm - Street, Tek, and Psi Judges
Manufactured by the Justice Department Armory, Sector 12.

TECHNICAL OVERVIEW
A semi-automatic, voice-encoded, DNA-locked sidearm - the standard-issue Judge weapon. Weighs 2.3 kg, measures 28 cm, and is built from a reinforced polymer-steel composite. Powered by a micro-cell battery that runs the voice recognition and ammo selector systems. Security is absolute - unauthorized use triggers a self-destruct charge within 0.5 seconds.

AMMUNITION TYPES
Selector 1 - Standard: 9mm high-velocity round for general enforcement.
Selector 2 - Ricochet: bounces off surfaces to hit indirect targets.
Selector 3 - Armour-Piercing: penetrates reinforced plating and light vehicles.
Selector 4 - Incendiary: ignites the target on impact.
Selector 5 - Hotshot: seeks heat signatures, used for precision termination.

OPERATIONAL NOTES
Voice commands ("Standard," "Ricochet," etc.) must match the Judge's registered vocal pattern. Grip sensors verify the wielder's genetic signature before firing. Tek Division recalibrates the voice module every 30 days. Early Mk I models are known to suffer selector lag under heavy smoke conditions.

HISTORICAL CONTEXT
Introduced in 2087 to replace the manual-selector Lawgun, and standard issue across Mega-City One by 2090. Mk II prototypes began testing in 2100, featuring digital ammo counters and improved ergonomics. The Mk I remains iconic - the weapon of choice during the Sector 21 pension riots and the SkyHigh Bank Heist suppression.

FIELD REPORT EXCERPT
"The Lawgiver Mk I doesn't ask questions. It listens, obeys, and judges."
- Judge Dredd, Armory Review 2099

records.name: Lex Luthor

records.name: Lotus Blossum
records.sub: Sector 21 · Sparkle Enterprise · Owner: Harry Jobby · 1 floors
records.details:
Lotus Blossum is a fashion accessory store for the wealthy. The store is a subsidiary of the Sparkle Enterprise company, which designs and makes clothing and body additions, as they're now referred to. Lotus has over 1,000,000 creds-a-week turnover and has been investigated on numerous occasions due to the owner putting Barry Welling in charge of one of the stores - a known ex-felon for stolen wares.



The owner of the company gave Barry the role after he was caught stealing from the shop to pay for his son's eye surgery. After doing iso-cube time, Barry was offered the job, and even after 4 years of on/off investigation, the shop and Barry remain clean.



Lotus Blossum is well known for the queue that forms outside every month on the 1st, as Harry Jobby's latest knee pad creation hits the store window.

records.name: Mahoney Moneybags
records.details:
Tall, mousey blonde hair and blue eyes. Dresses in suits always composed. No distinctive features visually however Mahoney has eidetic memory.

Moneybag's memory is astounding, it is said that he has an eidetic memory, meaning he has total recall. Mahoney is thought to do many accounts for the underworld, however he is clear in his employment that he does not know their ventures, only their accounts which separates him from their deeds. The Justice Department has tried a number of times to undermine his ability to represent companies with ties to criminal organisations however he is acutely aware of the law as well has accounts. Moneybags employs only the cleverest amongst MC1, they must all have a head for numbers and enjoy it. Moneybags is not linked to any criminal organisations, merely one of the best, if not the best auditors in MC1. In the criminal circles he's known as the Auditor of death as those that have been skimming (he always finds it) are often found dead, or never found at all. While he is aware of this, his only job is auditing accounts.

records.name: Manta Prowl Tank
records.details:
Judge-Only - Heavy Enforcement Vehicle - Riot & Block-War Deployment

The Manta Prowl Tank is the Judges' answer to anything too big, too loud, or too stupid for a Street Judge to handle alone. A Mega-City One enforcement machine, built for one thing: rolling into a riot and ending it.

CORE CHARACTERISTICS
Heavy Hover-Tank - The Manta doesn't use wheels - it hovers, allowing it to glide over debris, wreckage, and uneven block terrain. Its hover system is loud, deep, and resonant - citizens often describe hearing a Manta before seeing it.
Armored Hull - Thick composite plating designed to withstand small-arms fire, explosives, and makeshift riot weapons. Not invincible - but extremely hard to stop without military-grade firepower.
Crew - Minimum 4 Judges: Driver, Commander, Gunner, Support Judge (riot foam, crowd control, drone deployment).

OFFENSIVE & CONTROL SYSTEMS
Twin Cannons - Mounted on the front or upper hull depending on model. Used for block-war suppression, barricade destruction, and anti-vehicle action. Not subtle - when these fire, everyone in the block knows.
Riot-Foam Sprayers - High-pressure nozzles that blast expanding adhesive foam. Immobilizes crowds, vehicles, and fleeing perps. Tek Division handles cleanup because the foam hardens like concrete.
Drone Deployment Bays - Small enforcement drones for surveillance and crowd monitoring. Used to identify ringleaders or track fleeing suspects.

SUPPORT SYSTEMS
Floodlights - Mounted on the hull. Designed to blind, disorient, and expose rioters or looters.
Loudhailers - Built-in audio system for Judge commands. Can broadcast warnings, dispersal orders, or sentencing announcements.
Internal Judge Station - A cramped but functional command space. Used for triage, temporary detainment, or tactical planning.

records.name: Marcus Blackbone
records.details:
Black hair and blue eyes. Strong musclature, standing 6ft 5 he is imposing and every bit a Senior Judge of the Sector.

Marcus Blackburn is a Senior Judge of Sector 21, MC1. An exemplary career of 732 arrests in 14 years has seen Marcus become a respected judge throughout the sector. Marcus has a regular area on the west of the sector, and easier duties based on his track record and age. Liked by other judges, Marcus has occasionally been used for recruitment and training. Marcus is a Tech Judge, his senior status has seen him work on some of the most important cases in Sector 21. Specialising in micro components he has recently been involved in the investigation of Ewing amplifiers of Dallas Towers. The small company making music receivers had been substituting cheap chipset in favour of elite broadcasting units and selling them to the insanely rich elite who know no better than to pay their bills and show off their brand-new branded merchandise. Ceasar Ewing is currently a wanted fellon on the basis of Blackbone's investigation. Due to the recent lockdown of Dallas Towers, Caesar was able to escape capture. Should judges find Caesar his arrest warrant is issued. He's thought to have escaped the sector. Blackbone's investigations are thorough, he has been investigated by SGS only once, withstanding three days interrogation. As such, the SJS is convinced he has been involved in no wrongdoing.

records.name: Mary Glimmerfish
records.details:
A striking woman with flowing red hair that glows at the tips, in an armoured dark blazer-suit with a jewelled choker and green-piped trousers — cold, precise, and always immaculately turned out.

Mary began her career as a corporate negotiator before the Legal Purge of 2099, when all lawyers were declared illegal. Instead of disappearing, she adapted, rebranding herself as a "business mediator." Her firm, Glimmerfish Ltd, became infamous for resolving disputes that Judges considered beneath their notice.

Her clients range from block-war profiteers to rogue tech designers, and she's rumoured to have represented several known perps, always indirectly, always with plausible deniability. Technically legitimate, she remains under constant investigation by the Justice Department, though nothing has ever stuck.

Mary is cold, calculating, and surgically articulate. She speaks in clauses and sub-clauses, every sentence a contract, and her charisma is weaponised: she can make guilt sound like compliance. She isn't cruel, but she is pragmatic, having learned long ago that in Mega-City One compassion is a liability and survival depends on precision. Her office is immaculate, all glass walls and silver furniture, with a single Judge helmet mounted behind her desk, a trophy from a case she "won."

records.name: Maude Russel
records.details:
Palid in color - typical eldster with money - face lift's aplenty. Usually well dressed and has a mean streak a mile wide.

Maude is now a frustrated retiree in the El Supremo Plaza. Prior to enforced retirement she held many high ranking managerial roles before slowly with a wandering mind she was forced to give them up. Once arrested for assault of a judge when Selleck was sent to breakup a disturbance at the Job Centre. Selleck took it easy on her and limited the punishent, since then no issue and she `appears` happier

records.name: Max Impitus
records.details:
Well built, smart businessman normally dressed in a suit of some kind. Seems somewhat stressed at all times, but is one of the mega rich, so understandable. Loves the thrill of business. White hair and green eyes, athletic, 6ft2.

Forenzic accounting has audited Max already and found nothing unusual. The man loves the thrill of business and is all or nothing in his attitude. He has investments in huge industries but has recently sold them up, he looks to be consolidating to buy something large.

records.name: Max Investments
records.sub: Sector 21 · Max Investments · Owner: Max Max · 301 floors
records.details:
Max investments, where everyone is named max and they strive to make all the money that they can. 



Businesses all check out presently, but Tek judges monitor and carry out frequent audits. Tech in the building is state of the art and they are masters of the deal. 



Each Max looks to outdo others, even in the same building, although all the Max's will work together when needed.

records.name: Max Tarr
records.details:
Black hair, wears glasses, intelligent. Quick witted and slight of frame.

Not on the radar for any criminal actions, and has been recently passed for a police check by Mega Foods Inc

records.name: Mayri Shelley
records.sub: Sentient mimic droid, embedded as a Street Judge (deceased - sacrificed) · Age <Redacted>
records.details:
Outwardly an unremarkable Street Judge - the truth is she was never human at all.

Efficient, Shelley had an average record in Sector 21. When the new batches of young judges were rushed out to sectors, Sector 21 increased their Judge intake beyond the nominal number - several of the new Judges washed out, Shelley was one of the few that remained. She had good analytical skills but held on to cases longer than she should have.

It's since come to light that "Judge Shelley" was never a person at all - she was a sentient mimic droid, planted and run alongside Judge Joseph Dredd's own undercover operation to infiltrate the hidden Pegasus manufacturing plant beneath Rumbelows. Neither Shelley nor Dredd knew Pegasus's exact location going in. When Blue Team was cornered during the investigation, the Shelley droid chose to give its own life to save them - a genuinely sentient act of self-sacrifice from a machine no one suspected of being one. See the "Shelley Droid Sacrifice - Pegasus Infiltration" case file.

This also means every case Shelley personally reported or investigated - including the murders of Brian Ritter and Gremmil Stiener - was, in fact, run through an undercover asset working Dredd's own operation, not a conventional Judge. Worth a full case review.

records.name: MC1 News Network
records.details:
"Truth Is What We Tell You."

The MC1 News Network (MC1NN) is the official state-sanctioned broadcaster of Mega-City One - a sprawling, neon-lit complex of holo-screens, drone cameras, and propaganda towers. Its motto, "Truth Is What We Tell You," flashes across every broadcast.



From its headquarters in Sector 44, MC1NN controls all visual and auditory feeds across the city: news bulletins, riot alerts, celebrity executions, and Judge-approved entertainment. The network's anchors are half-celebrities, half-informants - smiling faces who deliver terror with charm. Primary exports: news feeds, propaganda, riot coverage, and Judge-approved entertainment.



The building itself is a towering prism of glass and steel, wrapped in holographic billboards showing Judge Dredd's silhouette and slogans like "Justice Never Sleeps." Inside, thousands of reporters, editors, and surveillance analysts work under constant scrutiny from the Media Control Division of the Justice Department.



MC1NN maintains an ongoing feud with the Undercity Pirate Broadcasters - illegal news crews who hack the network's feeds to broadcast anti-Judge messages.

records.name: McInley Medical
records.details: Not much is documented about McInley Medical beyond the fact that it's operating on medical technology decades out of date even by Gotham standards, and that its records show a genetic anomaly in an old in-vitro fertilisation program - primate DNA mixed into the process somehow, cause and outcome both unrecorded, or at least unreleased.

records.name: Mega Corp Campus
records.sub: Sector 21 · Mega Corp Campus · Owner: Wilson Merovingian · 451 floors
records.details:
The Mega Corp Campus houses many of the largest businesses in Sector 21. The massive building also includes a habitation zone for employees; this was built so that they did not need to vacate the building and could always work. Everything in this building is dedicated to work or business, including the habitation zone, which is designed to get the most out of the working citizens.



Employees of any of the businesses are often happy to be isolated within the building, given the resentment of people with jobs in Mega City One. The building produces its own food (not RESYK) and all other needs, as most businesses needed for living reside under its roof.



There is a special license within the building to only allow one of any type of business. This is thought to minimise financial espionage and allow the business owners to concentrate on growth and research. A special holiday zone resides in the centre of the campus - each employee is allowed one day in the zone per year.



Note that all contracts signed by the citizens are bullet-proof and escape-proof, and 100% legal according to tech judges and financial and law forensic panels.

records.sub: Sector 21 · Mega Food Incorporated · Owner: Milka Plenty · 329 floors
records.details:
One of the last food producers in S21 not linked to Resyk, the Mega Foods brand makes amazingly tasty food. 



Tek division have been over the company books and premises a number of times and the place is clean. No sugar or addictive additives and adequate security not to get broken into and cause the Sector House constant call out problems.

records.name: Mega-Tense
records.details: Mega-Tensile cabling is a product from Finger Enterprises. Its tensile strength is stronger than Synth-steel of double the circumference, however it’s expensive and only useful for industrial practices. The only company using high quantities is the MC1 Municipal Services. Uses include reinforcing rockcreet in high use zones. Most commonly in Super-Mega-Tensile, a thin wire that is used by Municipal Service window washing units for MC1 Blocks, the thin strands can support multiple Washbots on the block at any one time. This type of cable is also used in Judge jump ropes found in flying H-Wagons.

records.name: Mel House
records.details:
Blonde, glamourous, 5ft 3 and skinny. Bubbly personality with no distictive features.

Mel House is an ex-performer and entertainer. Her income from years of performing has enabled her an element of luxury at the El Supremo Plaza. For all intents and purposes she seems a lovely lady, genuine, and kind to all people that she meets. Mel still receives bags of fan mail from admirers both new and old. Where they get the video slugs of her performances is unknown!? Mel's performances included magic tricks, roller skating, dancing, hosting and interviewing. Mel is considered to be a model citizen. A career on the Tri-D was long and varied, however reports states that she was not happy losing her job to new performers after such an incredible career. Mel has been forensically investigated by tech judges only once however no criminal activities were picked up. It is suspected that Mel has various friends both in entertainment and the upper echelons of Sector 21.  Whether or not this is why she passed forensic accounts testing is unknown however she was never a high-priority. Mel is visited by her son weekly records show this is an ongoing event and does not change.

records.details:
Young, black hair and blue eyes, sharp but legit. She wants to enter the investing scene but can't find a way in.

Mel was investigated along side the audit of Max Impitus. Note the audit did not turn up anything on either her or her employer. She's completely focused and driven and looks to have attached herself to Max to get into investments one way or another. Whatever her future, it will be tied to him now, PSI evaluations state that she's frustrated at not being able to break into the market and she's getting more and more desperate.

Michael acres is a well-known chipset engineer and Is revered by tech judges and all IT companies including Rumbelows technology he works for. His chipsets are in a huge variety of applications from common household appliances to vehicles and weaponry. Rumblers has all trademarks and patents for his inventions and he seems happy enough about this, enjoying the challenge of creating new ideas for the company. Michael is not a doer he is an inventor and this is in his personal psyche as well making him incredibly lazy resulting in his divorce and only time in the iso-cubes when his apartment was so dirty that neighbours reported him for cleanliness violations. He was cubed for five months and allowed out only if he bought cleaning droids before taking residence back in Mega Corp Campus apartments. It's believed his apartment was fumigated three times before anybody else could live in it. Michael is the envy of most IT companies and they have tried to poach him (according to Michael) almost every week.  He has a strong devotion to Rumblers (unknown why).

records.name: Mobile Medibot
records.details:
A sleek red rover-style medical/utility vehicle on four chunky wheels, with a raised sensor turret bearing twin antennae and a white cross-adjacent chevron marking on its flank.

A compact, wheeled response unit built for speed rather than firepower, the Mobile Medibot is the first thing dispatched whenever a call comes in from an area with little to no reported danger. Its onboard processing is narrow but razor-sharp when it comes to medicine — diagnostics, triage, and field treatment are handled with a precision most human medics can only envy, even if it can barely hold a conversation about anything else.

Despite its size, the Medibot isn't confined to the quiet blocks. In a genuine emergency it can be scrambled into high-danger zones too, its armour plating and turn of speed letting it weave through the chaos of MC1 traffic almost untouched — citizen driving being, if anything, more hazardous than the crime scene it's racing towards.

That resilience is skin deep, though. Strip away the plating and the internals are delicate, densely packed medical hardware never designed to take a hit. For that reason the Judge Council has only ever signed off on deploying Medibots into non-combat situations — fast enough to get there, but built to heal, not to fight.

records.name: Moe Pearce
records.details:
Distinct limp and red scarring under left eye from Shuggy Hall brawl. Average height but frail. Brown hair and usually sports a moustache. Dresses in pinstripe suits and is generally affable.

Moe Pearce is a known to Sector 21 Judges. 20 years ago there was a Shuggy Hall War in which brawls were consistently broken up over the space of 2 weeks. Moe's was the last to survive the wars, the others torched and burnt out. He was cubed for violent assault when confronted by another owner who tried set fire to his hall. Instead of being involved in the larger brawl however he was prematurely spiked in the face with a cue stick losing his eye. While Moe was not proven to be involved in the destruction of the other halls' property, Moe's establishment then thrived as the only remaining place to play the popular game. There were discussions on removing the business under monopoly licencing, however Moe agreed to be part time peeper when being released from the cubes. The judicial department paid for his eye to be restored and replaced it with the latest opti-tech and it takes digital shots when judges require stakeouts for evidence material. (Note he is informed when this will happen for legal reasons.) Maybe for this reason, Moe is now clean.

records.name: Moes Shuggy Hall
records.sub: Sector 21 · Moes Shuggy Hall · Owner: Moe Pearce · 1 floors
records.details:
Moe’s shuggy Hall is a classy establishment catering to high end residents of Mega City 1. While betting is expected to happen within the hall, this low-level crime has escaped punishment as it is a low priority presently. 



The hall has passed all crime blitzes over the past two years. Moe’s seems to be clean, forensic tech judges have yet to prove any wrong doing within the building. Shuggy tables conform with strict regulations and no foul play found. 



Clientele is high-brow and a security bot deters trouble in the building. Note that there are now a few more Halls trying to establish themselves locally. Each of them seems to grow only so big before they close, siting nonprofitable performance. 

It is unclear whether this is linked directly to Moe, but judges expect him to have something to do with their closure.

3 years of hits means Mr Black is one of the most successful blitzers Sector 21 has known. Deacon Stroll has put warrants/rewards out to any informant with information on him. Mr Black has connections to multiple crime groups and doesn't stick with any in particular. Blitz-hits have been all over the Sector making tracking unpredictable. Mr Black plans meticulously leaving very few clues and even our best tech judges (Mathews) was unable to come up with useful evidence, however one piece of vid footage caught the assigned picture.

records.name: Municipal Building
records.details:
"Centralised Solutions for a Unified Sector."

The Municipal Building is a towering bureaucratic monolith responsible for managing all essential services for Sector 21: housing allocation, refuse processing, water distribution, power routing, sanitation drones, ration permits, and block maintenance. In theory, it is the beating administrative heart of the district. In practice, it is a catastrophic failure machine.



The building is staffed by tens of thousands of clerks, analysts, drone-techs, auditors, and "service coordinators," all drowning in paperwork, contradictory directives, and constantly changing regulations. Every few months a new policy is introduced that completely invalidates the previous one, causing entire departments to freeze while they wait for clarification that never arrives. Sector 21's blocks have tried, repeatedly, to break away from the central model and run their own services locally - each attempt lasts about three years before ending in chaos, corruption, or total collapse, at which point the blocks give up and return to the Municipal Building's centralised system, restarting the whole cycle of complaints, protests, and bureaucratic paralysis. Judges refer to the building simply as "The Tower of No."



Its functions cover housing assignment, water and power distribution, refuse and sanitation scheduling, block maintenance approvals, drone deployment, emergency resource rerouting, and complaint processing - the last of which is currently backlogged by fourteen years. At one time or another, every block in Sector 21 has held the Municipal Building responsible for something: Kowalski Block's water shortages, Ghett Block's refuse pile-ups, Skull-Hammer Heights' power rationing, The Melt's premature opening (still disputed), The Church's ritual scheduling conflicts, Kelly's News losing its broadcast license for 48 hours, and Glimmerfish Offices being denied additional floor space. Hostility rotates like a wheel - every block eventually becomes furious with the Municipal Building, then forgets, then becomes furious again.



The building rarely riots on its own, but it's a magnet for protest: angry citizens, block militias, religious groups, and disgruntled employees regularly gather outside demanding change, clarity, or simply someone to blame. Inside, the mood swings wildly with each new policy drop, system outage, drone malfunction, ration shortage, or mandatory morale assembly.



Chief among the building's recurring headaches is Fickle Garage, a notorious anti-establishment narcissist and self-styled "civil systems philosopher" whose slogan - "Let's go back to how it was!" - has powered decades of protest against "City Hall," despite the inconvenient fact that City Hall was demolished 47 years ago and replaced by the very building he protests outside of. Fickle leads weekly demonstrations, writes inflammatory pamphlets, and has been arrested 112 times for "administrative disruption." He is beloved by some, mocked by many, and feared by bureaucrats who know his speeches can turn a peaceful queue into a full-scale riot.

records.name: Municipal Housing Bureau
records.sub: Sector 21 · Municipal Building · Part of the Municipal Building's 294-floor structure floors
records.details:
"Housing Solutions for a Crowded Future."

The Municipal Housing Bureau (Sector 21 Office) is the nerve-frayed, overworked, perpetually collapsing sub-department responsible for assigning living spaces across Sector 21's mega-blocks. It occupies a sprawling multi-floor section of the Municipal Building and is widely regarded as the single most dysfunctional administrative unit in the district. Its mission is simple - "Assign housing fairly and efficiently" - and it has never once achieved it.



Citizens queue for hours, sometimes days, clutching holographic forms that flicker between DENIED, REVISE, and SEE FLOOR 212. Drones hover overhead, scanning applicants for fraud, emotional instability, or "queue aggression." The Bureau's staff - tens of thousands of clerks, analysts, and "allocation specialists" - drown in contradictory directives, outdated systems, and constant policy resets.



Every block in Sector 21 blames the Bureau for something: The Melt holds it responsible for the premature opening and collapse, The Church for ongoing ritual-space disputes, Glimmerfish Offices for a denied expansion. The Bureau is, in effect, the universal punching bag of the district - hostility rotates through it like a seasonal illness, and no one stays calm for long.



The Bureau itself rarely riots, but the citizens passing through it do, often. Queue fights, form-burnings, drone-smashings, and organised "allocation protests" are weekly events.

records.sub: Retired - Forced into retirement due to neglect of duty as Manager of El Supremo Plaza · Age 86
records.details:
Efficient business person, very intelligent and has run many companies as a capable CEO.

A very capable woman, mastering several businesses until achieving CEO at her first business. Whereupon she changed jobs frequently after bringing efficiencies and savings to each business she looked after. Nicknamed the hatchet, she was very effective, but little in the way of personal skills.

records.name: Nascar Block
records.details:
"Live Fast, Die Loud."

The Nascar Block is a vertical racetrack-city, a mega-block built around the cult of speed. Every floor is dedicated to motion - racing, tuning, betting, or worshipping the machine. The block's central shaft houses the Vertical Speedway, a spiraling 1.2km track that runs from the ground to the roof, where hover-cars, jet-bikes, and combustion relics scream through the air in endless loops.



Residents are obsessed with velocity. They wear racing suits as casual attire, decorate their apartments with engine parts, and measure status by horsepower. The block's motto, "Live Fast, Die Loud," glows in neon across its outer walls. It runs on hybrid plasma-combustion reactors and maintains a constant noise level averaging 140 dB.



Judges classify Nascar Block as a "High-Noise Hazard Zone." The roar of engines can be heard for kilometers, and riots often erupt when races are rigged or crashes block the shaft. The block holds active grudges against The Refinery, accused of selling low-grade fuel that caused mass engine failures; the Municipal Building, for enforcing noise restrictions; and Kelly's News, for broadcasting rigged race results.



Nascar Block is permanently on edge. Every race is a potential riot. Every crash is a block-wide event. The residents live for the sound of engines and the smell of burning fuel.

records.name: Neil Rochester
records.details:
Rochester has an athletic build, dark hair, slightly greying and blue eyes. He's clearly smart and thoughtful, a man of not many words.

Rochester has received 3 payouts from companies for accidents on their properties. In order not to sue the companies have agreed NDA agreements and paid him off. He seems to keep himself to himself, however he does seem to visit the BOING PINBALL often. Tek Judges have been unable to acertain the NDA agreements so these have yet to be confirmed real, or bribes/extortion.

records.name: Neural-Spectre Link
records.details: A short-range hacking rig wired directly into the brain, giving seamless neural integration with whatever it's aimed at. Co-created by Micka Pendell (operating under his "Mika Pendell" alias) and the entity known as J.C.N.2001, drawing on interface skills Micka honed during his years inside the Psych-Cubes. Originally built to pull information out of Mega-City One from J.C.N.2001's own dimension, the Link's real claim to infamy is that it eventually cracked M.A.C. itself - the Judges' central computer. It was deliberately handed off to a fall guy, Dillon Wellopstein, who used it to break into Finger Enterprises; Dillon was lobotomised and arrested almost instantly given Finger's ties to Sector House. On its own the Link only works at point-blank range against a target system, but combined with the Mega Bridge stolen from Finger Enterprises, its neurotransmitter signal was boosted enough to reach every Rumbelows robot in the city via the Nike-Spectre chipset that had quietly replaced their Azmov originals - turning the Link from a break-in tool into a citywide leash. Parts are now banned outright, and M.A.C. has since been patched with a reverse-engineered antineuronet to stop any repeat neurolink from forming with its core. See the "Neural-Spectre Link" case file for the full investigation.

Percy House is currently under investigation for links with criminal activities: Judge Shelley investigating. Percy seemed clean doing very little outside of his job until last year. On visiting a technology fair, Percy now visits technology companies and fairs often engaging with more and more people from that sector. He still visits his mother regularly in the El Supremo Plaza, this is a weekly event and has not changed. Recently Percy has been hanging around in Moe's Shuggy Hall, our investigation is ongoing and it does look like this is his new hobby. His game improves however he socially interacts as much as he plays in the environment. Percy's recent wider socialising is matched by his spending which now seems to be above his income even with his mother's charity. Where he is getting extra money from is unclear presently. Percy works at the Rise Up Garage, where he puts in many hours. The Rise Up Garage is under investigation for suspected chop shop activities, as such this may be the source of his new increased income. Rise Up Garage is under investigation by Judge Shelley (in her own time). The current whereabouts of Percy House are unknown the Rise Up Garage has been closed off for investigation and Percy seems to be the only survivor. Whether this was due to him not being there on the specific day of the massacre is unknown. Judges Smoke, Quinn, Asher, and Povey are investigating Percy's whereabouts.

records.name: Pinacalada McGee
records.details:
White hair, gold eyes. Tall and alwas well presented, she's slender and is quick witted.

Pinacalada has remained out of the public eye, which must have been difficult given Cheesy's popularity. Obviously wealthy she has no criminal record and keeps herself to herself. When appearing in public she has appeared standoffish and hides fromm the camera.

records.name: Pocket-Torch Microbeam
records.details:
Utility / Personal Gear

A palm-sized metal flashlight with chipped black paint revealing dull steel beneath. The cylindrical body has knurled grip rings worn smooth from years of handling. A single rubberized button sits near the top, slightly cracked, with dirt embedded around its edges.

The LED emitter is housed behind a small glass lens, scratched and fogged from pocket wear. When activated, it emits a sharp white beam that cuts through darkness with surprising intensity.

SPECIFICATIONS
Modes: Beam, Pulse, and SOS, indicated by tiny etched symbols. Battery: 12-hour micro-cell accessed via a screw-cap bottom. A soft click sounds when toggled, with a faint hum audible in pulse mode.

HISTORICAL CONTEXT
Distributed free during the Tunnel Collapse of 2083 to help citizens navigate blackout zones. As one civilian put it: "Light is survival."

records.name: Pretty Boy
records.details:
With a name like prettyboy what do you expect? Exceptionally charismatic standing 6ft and slim, he should be on the Tri-D.

Pretty boy is a renowned fixer Inside Dallas Towers. Priding himself on being able to get anything for any of the Dallas towers occupants he has made a name for himself. Prettyboy's negotiating skills are extraordinary, allowing him escape even from Judge retribution. As with most blocks, removing him would cause a void that could spark wide scale incidents within the building. Prettyboy's activities are mostly lawful and what indiscretions have been proven Are minor. He has a knack for finding the right people to fill the right needs, allowing him to stay away from unlawfully acquiring goods.   Pretty boy is confident and clever, it's only a matter of time before he realises what you need and with his army of contacts and people owing him favours he has the propensity to deliver. Pretty boy lives in Dallas Towers, however, it's not clear exactly where. It does appear however that he has many rooms for storage.

records.name: Prince Block
records.sub: Sector 21 · Prince Block · Owner: Roger Nelson · 139 floors
records.details:
Prince Block is dedicated to the 20th century musician. Considering themselves better in every way to the Michael Jackson Block, Prince residents are more outlandish, often taking things to the extreme. Prince block inhabitants pride themselves on being sophisticated and creative individuals.



This causes no end of problems - Prince Block demands its own sovereignty, for example. All inhabitants are dedicated to furthering the individualism of themselves, the building, prints, and anything else they can think of. The atmospheric station is set to rain 100% of the time over the small area that is this block. Purple tinted lights shine a hue through this. Significant?



Tenants of the block are often stroppy and want their own way. The block has had many wars with Michael Jackson Block, and both argue over the naming rights to Alphabet Street, with Michael Jackson Block arguing that it was originally ABC Street. Inhabitants are stylish, zany, and borderline psych-cube material.

records.name: Quin
records.details: An anthropomorphic ape in a black bowler hat and red-and-blue 3D glasses, dressed in an orange puffer vest over a plaid shirt — an eccentric, offbeat look.

records.name: Quinton Peal
records.details:
A clean-cut man with dark slicked-back hair and glasses, in a sleek white tech-lined coat over dark clothing — quiet, intense, and unsettlingly observant.

Known as "The Body Breaks. I Study How," Dr. Quinton Peal is Sector 21's foremost human biologist, a specialist in cellular breakdown under extreme environmental conditions, and one of the few scientists the Justice Department grudgingly respects. He operates out of the William Osler Block, a towering medical-research megastructure infamous for its morgues, trauma bays, and ethically questionable laboratories.

Peal is brilliant, clinical, and unsettlingly calm. He studies what Mega-City One does to the human body: radiation, pollution, stress, chemical exposure, block-war injuries, and the slow rot caused by living in a city that hates its citizens. Judges rely on him for forensic insight, but they also fear him; Peal understands human fragility better than anyone, and he's not shy about pointing out how easily the city could collapse.

Peal was once a standard med-tech researcher, but the Rad-Fog Incident of 2107 changed him. He survived exposure that killed dozens, and the cellular damage he sustained became the foundation of his life's work. Since then, he's devoted himself to understanding how Mega-City One destroys its people, and how to predict the moment a body fails. His lab is filled with samples of tissue exposed to every horror the city can produce: acid rain, chem-smog, rad-storms, nano-decay, and even stress-induced cellular collapse (a common condition in the city).

Peal is quiet, intense, and disturbingly observant. He speaks in clinical terms even when discussing casual topics, and has a habit of staring at people a little too long, as if analysing their cellular integrity. He's not cruel, but he's detached. To Peal, every person is a walking experiment in environmental stress. He often warns Judges that Mega-City One is "a petri dish with skyscrapers," and that humanity is the bacteria trying to survive.

Among citizens: "If you're falling apart, Peal can tell you why." Among Judges: "He's the best forensic biologist we have, and the most unsettling." Among scientists: "Peal studies the things we're afraid to admit exist." His reports have solved dozens of cases involving environmental murder, chemical sabotage, and biological tampering. He's also known for diagnosing Judges with stress-induced cellular degradation, a politically dangerous habit. Rumours claim he's developing a cellular resilience serum, but the Justice Department has classified all research notes.

His home block is a medical fortress: part hospital, part research lab, part morgue. It's filled with cryo-labs, biohazard vaults, trauma bays, environmental simulation chambers, and a Judge-only forensic wing. Peal's private lab is on Level 47, sealed behind biometric locks and guarded by med-drones.

records.name: Razor Electronics
records.sub: Sector 21 · Razor Electronics · Owner: Danny and Tess O'Sean · 9 floors
records.details:
Razor Electronics is known for producing yesterday's products at half the price. Both owners are constantly fighting claims of commercial espionage. Danny and Tess O'Sean are techs and founders of the company.



As a fledgling company, they landed the Vroom5, a turbo for cars that they could produce on a shoestring as an alternative to competitor Spark's expensive version. With the boom in jet packs made popular by the Aeroball games on TRI-D viewer, the turbo could be jury-rigged (illegal) to make significant improvements. Razor Electronics flourished through the sale of the units, stating they should not be used for such and avoiding prosecution.



The turbos were then banned by Judge Selleck; by then, Razor was already an established brand. ++Latest Project Classified++

records.name: Refinery
records.sub: Sector 21 · Refinery · 60 main levels + 12 sub-levels floors
records.details:
The Refinery is a vast industrial labyrinth where Mega-City One's waste becomes fuel and its fuel becomes waste again - both a power source and a dumping ground, a monument to efficiency and decay in equal measure. Built across nine square city blocks, it processes everything from bio-sludge and synthetic refuse to recycled plastics and corpse-fuel. Its towers belch flame and smoke day and night, painting the skyline in toxic orange, the air constantly humming with turbines, grinders, and chemical pumps.



Workers call it "The Furnace of Forever." Judges call it "Sector 21's necessary evil." Inside, thousands of labor drones and human operators toil under brutal conditions - the heat is constant, the air corrosive, and the ground trembles from the endless flow of molten waste.



The facility runs on self-sustaining plasma reactors fed by its own waste combustion, producing synth-fuel, bio-gas, organic fuel, recycled plastics, and corpse-fuel as primary output, and toxic runoff, airborne particulates, and black-smog residue as its inevitable secondary output. Security is handled by Judge-supervised industrial patrols and riot-response drones. The Refinery maintains an ongoing feud with the Municipal Building, over constant disputes involving waste quotas and safety violations.

records.name: Refinery+
records.details:
On the opposite side of Sector 21 from the old Refinery stands its successor: The Refinery+, a sealed, self-contained megastructure that no human being truly understands. Raw materials go in, finished products come out, and nobody outside the walls knows how. "If it exists, it came from the Plus," citizens joke, grimly, because it's often true.



The complex is completely sealed to human access. Logistics, distribution, and maintenance are entirely automated - drones, conveyor systems, and AI-controlled loaders handle everything from intake to export. The only human presence is a trio of liaison officers authorised to communicate with the Judges if required, though one recently died under mysterious circumstances. Rumours swirl that the deceased liaison was, impossibly, a version of "The Joker" from another dimension, who somehow crossed into Mega-City One through the facility's experimental quantum-matter conduits. The Justice Department denies this. The two surviving liaisons have refused to speak publicly since.



Inside, the Refinery+ is said to be a labyrinth of glowing corridors, automated assembly lines, and vast chambers where molecular printers and plasma forges reshape matter itself, running on a self-sustaining quantum-fusion core and producing everything from fuel and food to weapons, clothing, drones, and replacement organs. It's fully automated and fully sealed - Judges cannot enter without clearance, and there are no external access points beyond the material transfer ports.



The Municipal Building maintains an open grievance against it for refusing oversight and ignoring safety audits, and The Church calls it "a godless forge of false creation." Externally, the facility is calm. Internally, it's unknowable - no riots, no workers, no noise, only the hum of endless production.

records.name: Rise Up Garage
records.sub: Sector 21 · Rise Up Garage · Owner: James Cranium · 1 floors
records.details:
Found between Prince and Michael Jackson Blocks, the Rise Up Garage is under suspicion of being a chop shop for Mega City 1 vehicles. Nothing has been proven so far, as this is a minor concern at present. Should the company become bigger or be linked to a bigger organisation, this will be re-evaluated.



REVISION:: Gold Team have investigated a dead body outside the garage, leading to the discovery of 5 other bodies in the garage. Presently this is an ongoing investigation. Cause of deaths: SUICIDE. ++Further details classified: Sector Chief Judge Stoll++

records.name: Robert Minwell
records.details:
Middle aged gent, usually dressed in fine clothing. Black hair Green eyes and heavy build.

Robert Minwell is Sector 21's biggest media mogul. Robert's fortune is immense, making him almost untouchable as a citizen of Sector 21. His contacts throughout the upper and lower echelons of Sector 21 are unsurpassed through years of reporting and investigating both the rich and criminal of MC1. Robert is known throughout MC1 as the news franchise that stood up to judges, holding them accountable. As such whilst the judicial system is under his spotlight Minwell needs to be handled carefully. Robert's investigations, through Cheesy McGee lately, have resulted in a number of crime blitzes and arrests. In breaking high-level stories he received several awards and was in the right place at the right time to pick up the top job in sector 5, MC1 News. Using his new wealth he bought the little known Sector 21 franchise and has never looked back, uncovering the infamous Judge Claren assassination and "Big Kook-Up" Scandal before judges had resolved their investigations.

records.name: Robin
records.details: A young masked hero in a red, black and gold costume with a black-and-yellow cape and a bold yellow 'R' emblazoned on the chest.

records.name: Robo Dogs
records.details:
A sleek, armoured quadruped robot built along wolf lines, with glowing yellow eyes and oversized, saber-tooth-style fangs.

Fast, aggressive, and built to intimidate as much as to pursue — Robo Dogs are used as security and hunting units by those who can afford them.

records.name: Roger Apples Tango Ltd
records.details:
Roger Apples Tango Ltd runs a single floor and eight employees, and on paper it's exactly what the signage says: a small, tax-paying purveyor of fruit and fruit-adjacent goods. Nobody at Roger Apples Tango Ltd will confirm, deny, or otherwise discuss what the company actually does, because nobody wants to be the block that admitted it had a pest problem. The name does the marketing so the branding doesn't have to: cheerful, wholesome, entirely unrelated to the fact that R.A.T. is an extermination outfit, and a thorough one.



That thoroughness got noticed recently, when a Roger Apples Tango callout to the El Supremo Croc block ended with two entire floors of residents dead. The subsequent investigation didn't land on the company - it landed on two individuals allegedly responsible: a tall, skinny, brown-haired male in a trench coat, and an accomplice described, without anyone quite managing to say it with a straight face, as a white-or-orange-furred monkey in a blue gilet and orange shirt. Roger Apples Tango's official statement maintains the two have no connection to the company whatsoever. The Judges have yet to locate either of them to ask.

records.sub: Sector 21 · Rumbelows · Owner: Basil Rumbelow · 83 floors
records.details:

Rumbelows holds key robot stock for all MC1 robots. The building is sanctioned for security to use deadly force if attacked. All other information classified - contact Judge Joseph Dredd.

records.details:
Charasmatic eldster. Hunched and frail, showing his age, Saul has grey hair now and walks with a cane. It's believed that he has a heart condition.

Saul Bloom Looks after Procurement for the company, why this is not trusted to a robot, given they make  Quartermaster robots, this is unclear. His procurement practices often revolve around other individuals rather than computers, all their accounts seem to be by hand rather than computer which while strange seems to still stack up. Saul is wiley, you will often start talking to him trying to find out information and instead and up telling him what he wants to hear. He is generous with his time to other employees and even us Judges.

records.name: Sector House
records.sub: Sector 21 · Sector House 21 · Owner: Judicial Department · 216 floors
records.details:
Sector House 21 is located in the centre of Sector 21 of Mega City 1. One of the largest buildings in the sector, it is close to arterial routes through the sector. Most of the sector's Judges are located at this building.



Containing garages, arsenal, M.A.C., sleep chambers, call centre, and training facility, the Sector House is a central point for communications for the whole sector. State of the art training facilities include full fumigation/extinguishers for Stumm Grenade/explosive practice.



Air vents simulate bigger blocks of MC1, and bomb disposal/tactical resolutions are often planned there. Equipment resources are circulated from the central room, as provisions offices are located directly below.
