records.name: Security Bot Mark 2
records.details:
Three red eyes in a glass dome are a distinctive characteristic of this killer bot. Double jointed legs and more humanoid than the Mark 1.

The Mark 2 is an improvement on the Mark 1 security bot with more human characteristics in some respects, adapting to urban pacification. Reasoning capabilities are minor - this is purely a seek-and-destroy robot. With more human characteristics this machine can use any human weapon as well as an additional proprietary weapon. Legs are double jointed much like an animal's to improve stability. Speed for these units was also improved, especially over rough terrain. Strength has been improved as well as agility. These units can be used for both protection and attack, requiring anyone using them to have special dispensation licenses. There are 25 units in MC1 Sector 21 - it is not clear if this is due to cost or simply the difficulty in applying for them.

records.name: Security Bot v1
records.details:
Bipedal mechanised warrior robot. Able to handle a variety of weapons.

This mechanised unit has arms and hands allowing it to use a variety of weapons including human hand weapons and heavy alternatives usually limited to vehicles. Many businesses/individuals are now able to purchase these units at a cheap price as bigger businesses replace them with the Mark 2 and upcoming Mark 3 models. The processing power of these units is slow by today's standards for security bots, however they were state of the art when they appeared on the market. Very accurate with shooting capability but their reasoning is somewhat limited. There are thousands of these units within MC1. These units include a pacification command as a subroutine that allows any current judge to immobilise the robot. As with all robots, their owners/masters are culpable for the actions of the robot.

records.name: Security Bot v2
records.details: A hulking black-and-gold combat robot with glowing red optic sensors, heavy shoulder and thigh armour plating, and an integrated weapon mounted on one forearm.

records.name: Shauna White
records.details:
Black long hair, slender tall build. Bubbly and charasmatic, perfect for the Tri-D. No distinguishing features, but is recognised by most Sector 21 citizens

Shauna White is the "MC1 News weather girl". Shauna has an incredible following given her performances whilst delivering the weather. Social networking, criminal referencing and poignant commentary on city ongoings are all parts of her delivery method. It is well known she is on the fast track for becoming a reporter, whether this is good for the Justice Department is a matter of concern, one Cheesy McGee is enough! Shauna is earning a reasonable amount of credits as a weather girl, and her spending is in-line and proportion with that pay. No investigation has been made of Shauna however as she climbs in status it is likely that this will be necessary. Shauna seems talented and aggressively propels her career upward. Due to her subtle leaks of information RE the elite of MC1, Shauna underwent (unknown to her) a PSYCH test. This uncovered nothing, she is now suspected to have extremely good connections rather than any psychic ability.

records.name: Simpsons Block
records.sub: Sector 21 · Simpsons Block · Owner: Bart XXXI · 200 floors
records.details:
A manic building on the precipice of riot. They write their own rules... literally, and the answer to everything is "don't have a cow"! If caught doing something, the citizen has to write 200 lines of whatever the current reigning Bart states to write.



All citizens are required to look like one of the popular 90s TV show's characters, which makes finding anyone in the building difficult - they all look the same. All building inhabitants are required to get into trouble of some sort each day. Note: Homers are special, they will only respond with "Doh!"



Everything is yellow and blue, and that music!!! Note the inhabitants continue to petition for breaking clouds above the building daily.

records.name: Skull-Hammer Heights
records.details:
"Strength Is Law."

Skull-Hammer Heights is a fortress-block obsessed with strength and survival. Its residents worship the idea of "hammer justice," believing brute force is the only law that matters. The building itself looks like a war machine - reinforced plating, turret emplacements, and a massive skull-and-hammer emblem carved into its upper facade.



Inside, every floor is a training ground: gyms, weapon ranges, and "discipline chambers." The block's militia, the Hammer Guard, patrols constantly, enforcing curfews and mandatory combat drills. Judges consider it one of the most dangerous blocks in the city - not because it's chaotic, but because it's organized violence.

records.name: Skull-Hammer Heights Legal Syndicate
records.sub: Sector 21 · Skull-Hammer Heights · 12 (within Skull-Hammer Heights) floors
records.details:
"Law Is War."

The Skull-Hammer Heights Legal Syndicate is the judicial extension of the militant mega-block Skull-Hammer Heights, where law and warfare are indistinguishable. Its lawyers are combat veterans turned litigators, suited in black armor-weave business attire, each wearing a bandolier of legal cartridges containing case files, evidence chips, and tactical injunctions.



They operate from fortified offices on the upper floors of Skull-Hammer Heights, where courtrooms resemble command bunkers and verdicts are delivered like airstrikes. Their motto, "Law Is War," is etched above the entrance in steel letters. Standard kit runs to stun-briefcases and drone bailiffs alongside the armored suits and bandoliers.



The Syndicate specialises in contract enforcement, corporate warfare, and retaliatory litigation. They represent Skull-Hammer interests in every dispute, from property rights to block-war reparations, and are infamous for turning legal hearings into psychological combat. They maintain an ongoing feud with Glimmerfish Offices over jurisdiction and ethics, and hold the Municipal Building in open contempt for what they call "bureaucratic cowardice."



The Syndicate thrives on conflict. Every case is treated like a campaign, every courtroom a battlefield - their lawyers shout, strategize, and deploy arguments like artillery.

records.name: SkyHigh Bank
records.sub: Sector 21 · SkyHigh Bank · Owner: Chester Dribblethwait · 16 floors
records.details:
The SkyHigh Bank is a mobile bank that secures itself overnight by perching on the "Bank Tether," over 300 floors up in the city. The bank's security is thought to be impregnable and state of the art. During the day, people are free to enter and conduct business at ground level.



Then, at the end of a business day, automated systems shuttle the whole bank to the Tether. On top of the bank lies a huge amount of firepower, all legal. There is a no-fly zone around the Tether, and cars are often given a warning jolt if they get too close.



It is thought that several Sector 21 elite citizens use the vault's Maxi-Safe storage, although the bank is open to anyone that has even a few creds.

records.name: Slab-Loaf Nutrient Brick
records.details:
Food / Low-Block Sustenance

A dense, rectangular nutrient loaf sealed inside a dull grey foil wrapper that's always slightly greasy to the touch. The foil is thin and crinkled, with heat-seal seams running unevenly along the edges - some packs show tiny burn spots from cheap factory sealers. The front bears a faded red stamp reading "NUTRI-LOAF - GOV ISSUE," misaligned as if printed by a machine that hasn't been serviced in decades.

Inside, the loaf itself is a beige, chalk-like block with a faint synthetic sweetness. The surface is dry and crumbly, with tiny air pockets and darker flecks of vitamin slurry. When broken apart, it sheds powder that clings to fingers and clothing.

COMPOSITION
Synth-starch base, vitamin paste, trace protein, stabilizers. Smell: neutral with a hint of plastic. Texture: dense, gritty, slightly rubbery when warmed.

OPERATIONAL NOTES
Can be eaten cold or warmed on a heat-coil strip. Crumbles easily, leaving residue everywhere. Often cut into chunks and traded in informal block markets.

HISTORICAL CONTEXT
Became the primary ration during the Sector 5 Crisis of 2082, when supply chains collapsed. As one civilian put it: "It fills you up. That's all it promises."

records.name: Small Carpark
records.details:
A cramped, low-rise carpark of the kind bolted onto the side of just about every block in Sector 21 - a single open level or two, undersized for the number of vehicles that try to squeeze in, with a payment terminal that's been vandalised more times than it's been repaired.



Quiet, unremarkable, and largely unpoliced. Exactly the kind of place nobody looks twice at, which is precisely why it keeps turning up in places it shouldn't.

records.name: Snack-Tube Cruncher
records.details:
Food / Packaged

A cylindrical plastic tube with neon graphics peeling from the surface. The pop-cap is flimsy and often cracks, causing chips to spill. Inside, the synth-chips are brightly colored and dusted with fluorescent powder that clings to skin.

The chips themselves are thin, brittle, and extremely loud when bitten - a side effect of the aerated synth-starch used in production.

FLAVORS & HAZARDS
Salt-Blast, Cheese-Synth, and Fire-Crunch varieties. Texture: crunchy, brittle, dust-coated. Hazards: tube cracking, powder staining, addiction.

HISTORICAL CONTEXT
Popular during the Block Games of 2085. As one civilian put it: "Crunch loud enough to drown out the neighbors."

records.name: Sparkle Enterprises
records.sub: Sector 21 · Sparkle Enterprises · Owner: Harry Jobby · 21 floors
records.details:
Sparkle Enterprises is a well known company specializing in high end designer merchandise. The company founder, Harry Jobby, still creates new knee pads on a monthly schedule, selling them through their Lotus Blossum store and making millions yearly.



Sparkle distributes through other elite stores, but in Sector 21, just through his store chains. Sparkle also designs other clothing, specialising in Authentic-Spec-Wear: custom clothing for the stars, replicating clothing seen in old movie slugs.

records.name: Spiritex
records.details: Uncommon cleaning material made by Clinical Componex. Highly flamable and only manuafactured and distributed for medical and clinical practices.

records.name: Spoon
records.details:
Pink mohawk and minimal clothes. Acompanied by mirrorlike idiots

Spoon, fork, and whisk are triplets from a disturbed marriage between two disturbed individuals. The triplets quickly fell in with the wrong crowd and have been cubed more times than they've had birthdays. To say they are stupid is an understatement, Dredd thinks they share an IQ between them. And the one that has it, is never the one he meets at any given time. Most of their crimes have been simple robbery or taps. Over the past few months/year they have not been in the cubes, judge Cullis as an open question with the Street judges of Sector 21 as to whether they have been killed either  by their own stupidity or by some other gang. Always supporting the same haircut and very few clothes, The pink Pukes as they like to be called are easily recognisable. Report to Cullis any sightings.

records.name: Street Judge
records.details: A Judge in classic gold-shouldered armour and red-and-white helmet, sidearm holstered and a Lawgiver pistol in hand.

records.name: Street Judge Ration Pack
records.details:
Active Service (All Divisions) - Street, Tek, and Med Judges
Manufactured by the Justice Department Armory, Sector 12.

TECHNICAL OVERVIEW
Contents: synthetic protein slab, caffeine gum, a hydration capsule, and a morale chip (plays "I Am the Law" when bitten). Weighs 0.6 kg with a 5-year shelf life when sealed. Sustains a Judge through 12 hours of active patrol or riot duty. Taste profile per Judge Anderson's 2098 Review: "Industrial nutri-paste with undertones of despair."

HAZARDS
Overconsumption may cause temporary aggression and compulsive statute quoting. Store below 40C - exposure to heat may trigger the morale chip prematurely.

HISTORICAL CONTEXT
Introduced after the Block War Famine of 2095 to replace the Mk II packs, which melted under Lawmaster exhaust heat. The Mk III added caffeine gum and the morale chip to combat fatigue and psychological strain during extended patrols.

FIELD REPORT EXCERPT
"It's not food. It's fuel. And sometimes, that's all the Law needs."
- Judge Dredd, Sector 21 Briefing 2099

records.name: Street-Noodle Brick
records.details:
Food / Street Vendor

A tightly compressed noodle block sealed in silver foil with a tear-tab that often snaps off. The foil is printed with bright red text reading "STREET-NOODLE - JUST ADD WATER," though the ink is smudged on most packs. A small seasoning packet is taped to the side with cheap adhesive that leaves residue.

The brick itself is pale yellow, with visible noodle strands fused together. When rehydrated, it expands into a bowl of rubbery noodles with uneven texture.

FLAVORS & TEXTURE
Spicy-Synth, Soy-Salt, and Mega-Curry varieties. Smell: strong artificial seasoning. Texture: chewy, occasionally crunchy in the center.

OPERATIONAL NOTES
Vendors rehydrate using questionable water sources. Overheating causes the noodles to become rubbery. Often eaten directly from the foil.

HISTORICAL CONTEXT
Became a staple during the Block Famine of 2084. As one civilian put it: "Cheap, fast, filling - the holy trinity."

records.name: String Bean
records.details:
Slight, wiry, forgettable build - the kind of person you lose track of even while staring at them. Real identity unknown; witnesses describe her only as "that thin one... I think."

One of those ghosts of Sector 21 - always seen, never remembered, which is exactly how she likes it. Her greatest suspected feat is the SkyHigh Bank Heist, pulled off during the infamous Sector-wide blackout: the bank's automated headcount system logged her as "out" while she was still very much inside, letting her remain in the vault overnight as the entire bank detached from the tower and rose to its tethered perch 300+ floors above Mega-City One. By morning she was gone, along with several high-value data chips and a handful of physical currency notes. Investigators believe she exploited her slight frame, a blind spot in the bank's thermal sweep, and the blackout's temporary override of biometric redundancy - and possibly dumb luck, though Judges hate writing that in reports.

Modus operandi: slips into places unnoticed, stays still for hours, moves only when shadows move, prefers data-chips over physical goods, and never leaves fingerprints - possibly gloves, possibly (per rumour) because she doesn't have any. Judges suspect she works alone, since no one else remembers seeing her either. One Judge described her as "a draft with shoes." See the "SkyHighBank Heist (String Bean)" case file - still open, no team assigned.

records.name: Stumm Gas Canister
records.details:
Restricted - Crowd Control Device - Standard Riot-Control Issue - Street and Riot Judges
Manufactured by Tek Division, Mega-City One Armory.

TECHNICAL OVERVIEW
A non-lethal aerosol dispersal device. Weighs 0.9 kg, an 18 cm x 6 cm cylinder built from a reinforced alloy shell with a ceramic seal. Activated by a twist-cap and voice-coded trigger ("Stumm Gas - Deploy"). Effective radius of 20m, with 60 seconds of active dispersal followed by a 5-minute residual effect.

COMPOSITION
Agent: poly-stumm aerosol compound. Induces unconsciousness within 3-5 seconds of inhalation, with full consciousness returning after 10-15 minutes. Judges must wear sealed helmets when deploying - exposure without filtration causes temporary paralysis.

OPERATIONAL NOTES
Used for riot suppression, hostage rescue, and crowd pacification. Deployment is authorized only under Code Red Riot Protocol. Tek Division handles post-event decontamination. Canisters are single-use, disposed of via the Armory reclamation chute.

HISTORICAL CONTEXT
Introduced in 2085 after the Block War Riots, replacing the earlier "Sleep Gas" models due to faster onset and cleaner dispersal. Standard issue for all Street Judges by 2090. Commonly deployed from Manta Prowl Tanks or handheld launchers.

FIELD REPORT EXCERPT
"One canister, one minute, one block silent."
- Judge Dredd, Sector 21 Riot Log 2099

records.name: Subway
records.details:
A standard stretch of Sector 21's underground transit network - tiled platforms, flickering route boards, and the permanent smell of ozone from trains that run just often enough to keep the crowds from turning ugly. Judges patrol in pairs down here, less out of duty than out of the certainty that something is always about to happen.



Every subway station in the sector looks and feels much the same: cramped, echoing, faintly hostile, and the fastest way to get anywhere that matters.

records.name: Tek Judge
records.details: A Judge in blue-and-gold armour with a red-and-white helmet marked 'TEK', wielding an oversized scanning device against a Justice Department backdrop.

records.name: Terrance Zod
records.details:
Dark brown hair, balding at the front. Blue eyes. Middle aged. Often look dishevelled.

Terrance Zod is a recent acquisition for the Mahoney Moneybags Auditors. As a hard-working accountant he was reference by Gremmil Stiener. Forensic examination of his accounts and accounting practices have turned up nothing. Zod does accounts for fun, often not charging for his services in his free time. Zod owns an accounting robot, his biggest asset, and this is used to promote his accounting hobby. As yet he has never been approached by a criminal organisation for his accountancy expertise, however this is an ongoing threat and under review. Whether we stop Zod's spare-time accounting and ask him to pick a different hobby is a source of concern for his free will at the moment! Zod has no family members remaining alive and as an exemplary employee at the company.

records.name: The Batman
records.details:
Blue and black spandex with a cowl covering his face, and a large cape. Physically peak shape.

Not a lot known about the Batman. Bill Finger is linked to the man. We've been told he fights superpowered beings in his dimension. He has a secret identity in Gotham. It's thought that his gadgets and Bill Finger's gadgets might be linked now that we know of this person. Who's gadgets they actually are, we'll need to find out.

records.name: The Joker
records.details:
Makeup like a maniacal clown with green hair. Often dressed in purple suit. Stronger and quicker than he looks and is armed.

Not much known about the Jokerother than evil and ingenious. Thought to be the antithesis of Batman however we only have Bill Finger hearsay for this. The joker is thought to be incredible dangerous and insane.

records.name: The Melt
records.details:
"We Endure. (added after the collapse)"

The Melt is one of the most notorious architectural catastrophes in Sector 21's history. Originally intended as a cutting-edge "rapid-set residential block," it was constructed using an experimental material called plasticrete - a polymer-infused concrete designed to harden in hours instead of weeks.



Municipal oversight failed spectacularly. Before the plasticrete had fully set, the city advertised the block as "Move-In Ready," triggering a flood of eager citizens desperate for housing. Within days, three entire floors liquefied, sagged, and collapsed into each other like wet clay. Thousands were crushed, suffocated, or trapped in the slurry-like structural failure. The disaster became known simply as The Melt, and the block has never escaped the name.



The architect responsible, Dr. Halden Voss, was sentenced to 30 years in Iso-Cubes. He maintains to this day that the structure would have been perfectly safe if the Municipal Housing Bureau hadn't prematurely opened the doors and "turned a curing building into a stampede." Plasticrete was banned citywide within 48 hours of the collapse.



The block now runs reinforced "post-melt" support struts, a memorial atrium on Floor 12, permanently sealed lower levels (Floors 18-20), and structural monitoring drones that never stop scanning. Residents remain openly hostile toward the Municipal Housing Bureau's Sector 21 Office, which they blame for the premature opening and the deaths - Bureau drones are routinely vandalised near the block.



The mood inside is best described as brittle stability: tense but not riotous, fiercely protective of home, and quick to anger at outsiders who mock the disaster. The trauma lingers as a simmering emotional volatility. Whatever hostility exists is conducted well outside the building - inside, everything is handled with as little movement, shift, and bounce as possible.

records.name: Titan Mining Corporation
records.sub: Sector 21 · Titan Mining Corporation · Owner: Judicial · 21 floors
records.details:
The Titan Mining Corporation is a large corporation based around the small planet's dealings with Earth. All correctional facility details, protocols, manufacturing, and purchasing is handled in these offices.



The building has high security and handles all business with the planet directly, not needing M.A.C. to deal with the offsite Judges. There will always be a small number of Judges assigned to the building, as the guards on planet cycle off world.



The building includes processing and refinery machinery. TMC owns a huge fleet of vehicles to transport in raw material, as well as distribute ores etc.

records.name: Turkish Elation Malloy
records.details:
Slick, everything about Turkish is about the long con. Several judges have tried to take him down but he's a slippery eel.

Turkish grew up in the slum areas of the Sector. He's made a name for himself planning cons so successfully that when they're busted he still can't be linked to them. Polite, unobtrusive and careful with his words he knows the law and he knows the people he deals with. He's been under surveillance several times, but to no avail. Wally Squad reports that he's been seen with other suspected Tommy Gunn members, whether he's a memeber of the gang or not is open to question. As yet no evidence is linkable to Turkish. The only time he's done time in the cubes is littering in the slums! On reflection that seemed like a way to get a fresh meal rather than a warranted arrest. Turkish is friendly with Gorgeous George who is in and out of the cubes, however he seems friendly with everyone.

records.name: Undercity Pirate Broadcasters
records.details:
"Truth Unfiltered. Signal Unbound."

Deep beneath Sector 21, in the cracked tunnels and forgotten maintenance shafts of the Undercity, the Undercity Pirate Broadcasters operate their rogue transmission network known as Free Vox. They are the unseen voices of rebellion - journalists, hackers, and ex-media technicians who hijack official feeds to broadcast uncensored news, Judge raids, block wars, and conspiracy exposes.



The collective's studios are cobbled together from scavenged tech - hacked drones, jury-rigged transmitters, and salvaged MC1NN equipment. Their feeds are unstable but addictive, mixing real footage with propaganda and rumor. Citizens tune in secretly, knowing that being caught listening can mean a trip to the cubes. The Justice Department classifies Free Vox as a Class-3 Information Threat, but every time they shut down one transmitter, three more appear.



Known channels include Free Vox, Truthline, BlockCast, and The Melt Feed, broadcasting leaked Judge footage, block war coverage, anti-bureaucratic rants, corruption-exposing "Truthcasts," and pirate entertainment feeds, reaching up to twelve blocks when the signal isn't jammed. The network carries an open feud with MC1 News Network, which brands them "terrorists with microphones," and with Glimmerfish Offices, after airing leaked case files.



The collective thrives on adrenaline and paranoia - every transmission could be their last. They live in constant fear of Judge raids, signal jamming, and betrayal from within.

records.name: Vid-Player 2089 Compact
records.details:
Discontinued - Civilian Use Only
Manufactured by Omni-Media Corp., Sector 17.

TECHNICAL OVERVIEW
A portable holographic video player with a 12cm holo-lens and adjustable projection depth. Runs off a micro-cell battery good for 36 hours of playback, with 128GB of crystal-core memory. Connects via data-jack or short-range beam-link, and outputs audio through dual-channel spatial emitters.

OPERATIONAL NOTES
Plays Holo-Vid, Flat-Vid, and Retro 2D formats. Controlled via a touch-strip interface or voice command ("Play," "Pause," "Rewind"). Polish the lens weekly, and keep it away from BOING residue.

HISTORICAL CONTEXT
Released during the Post-Broadcast Era, when personal holo-media replaced centralized feeds. Became a cultural icon among collectors for its retro-chrome casing and analog toggle switch.

CIVILIAN REVIEW EXCERPT
"Still the best way to watch Singin' in the Rain when the block's power grid collapses."
- Citizen Review Board, 2090

records.name: Vince Cherwell
records.sub: Refinery specialist - now assisting the Gold Judge team (formerly unemployed waste-processing operator)
records.details:
Recently unemployed. Spent years processing bodily waste at the Refinery, where the rusted-up robots meant the worst of the work fell to him - a job he only took to qualify for benefits, but grew to find a strange sense of purpose in. Stinks badly enough from years on the job that he's been shunned even outside working hours.

The Refinery's main tank has been repurposed for a different mixing process, and Vince's job processing bodily waste is gone with it. He'd taken the position because it was the only way to qualify for benefits, but says he'd since learned to enjoy the work - now he's lost that too, and doesn't see much point without it.

Vince has moved in to live at the Refinery itself - he stank so badly from the job that he was shunned at Dallas Towers, his previous address.

records.name: Virgil Mulloy
records.details:
Smooth talker, and smart dresser. Brown hair, blown eyes. 5ft 9 and slim build

Hasn't been investigated and doesn't have any arrest warrents. He's clean at the moment but so smooth that it has to be hiding something.

records.name: Walter the Wobot
records.details: Shares its design with Evil Ruth — the same silver-grey humanoid frame with a glowing red-eyed screen-face and 'TRY ME' chest plate — though Walter is usually pictured against an industrial, orange-lit backdrop rather than Ruth's plain setting.

records.name: WarBot Mark 1
records.details:
No humanoid characteristics, looking more like a mechanoid chicken with two legs and a blocky body with large armament strapped to the sides.

Razor Electronics' WarBot Mark 1 is a somewhat inferior version of the Security Bot Mark 1 produced by Rumbelows. An old, but popular model in MC1, they are cheaper but less mobile than the Rumbelows version. Coming in a variety of colours, the robot is somewhat clumsy but supports mega firepower and armour. This unit contains a pacification subroutine that allows judges to immobilise the robot. The Mark 1 is preferred for sentry duty and contains voice recognition and biometrics to determine hostiles. There are thousands of the Mark 1 model around Sector 21 alone. Many vid-slugs of the Mark 1 comically portray the bot on its side, having been knocked off its feet and unable to stand up. While this vulnerability is absolutely true, the bot is very heavy, so to move it and make it fall over is somewhat hard - and not forgetting the hail of bullets it can send your way as you're trying it.

records.name: WarBot Mark 2
records.details:
A tiny head sunk in a huge armoured shell. Both feet and hands are claw-like. 7ft tall.

The WarBot Mark 2 is the second version of the popular model. Maintaining a bipedal appearance, the unit now has a body and limbs, although these limbs are not dextrous, with claws rather than hands connected to the upper limbs, limiting the weaponry to proprietary versions of popular guns. Armour is incredibly strong on this unit and guns are hidden until required. These units are mostly made for sentry duty and are able to take a battering whilst still delivering a substantial payload to any hostile. Reasoning has been improved with these machines, making their brainpower superior to the Rumbelows models. One of the cheapest security bots on the market, the Mark 2 is often bought by businesses to protect valuable locations. This machine weighs a considerable amount as armour is prioritised. As with all robots, this mech contains a pacification mode that can be engaged by any current judge.

records.name: Whisk
records.details:
Pink mohawk and minimal clothes. Accompanied by mirrorlike idiots

Spoon, fork, and whisk are triplets from a disturbed marriage between two disturbed individuals. The triplets quickly fell in with the wrong crowd and have been cubed more times than they've had birthdays. To say they are stupid is an understatement, Dredd thinks they share an IQ between them. And the one that has it, is never the one he meets at any given time. Most of their crimes have been simple robbery or taps. Over the past few months/year they have not been in the cubes, judge Cullis as an open question with the Street judges of Sector 21 as to whether they have been killed either  by their own stupidity or by some other gang. Always supporting the same haircut and very few clothes, The pink Pukes as they like to be called are easily recognisable. Report to Cullis any sightings.

records.name: Will Shatner Block
records.sub: Sector 21 · Will Shatner Block · Owner: Federation of Planets (Enterprise) · 104 floors
records.details:
Will Shatner Block is a somewhat large block dedicated to the famous actor of the 60s, 70s and 80s. Given the actor's wide range of roles and the enormity of them, the building's theme is widespread. Every business in the building has the suffix Enterprise.



The outside of the building has a mountain face on one side, and climbers ascend this side of the building using the appropriate equipment, trademarked 'Klingon' apparatus, made by Klingon Enterprises. The building has rich and poor areas, the front being somewhat of a facade for the rich, and the back and lower floors somewhat more seedy.



Star Trek of the 60s and 70s is a theme within the building for those that buy vid-slugs on the black market. Any citizens believing in UFOs bringing the end of the world (while this may be the case) can be found in this building preaching the primary directive. At some point Sector Judge Stoll has promised to take the primary directive (the Law!) to these individuals, break them up, and distribute them around the sector in other blocks.



A majority of the citizens within the building wear uniforms based on the TV show, and there is unceremonious fighting between individual factions preferring one show over another. Face change businesses do more business converting ears to be pointy(?!?) than they do face changing operations. There is also an increased amount of green pigmentation changes for citizens.



It was thought that we should ban this practice, given it slows the identification of infectious diseases. However, recent ugly practices seem to have diluted this action. The block is generally a passive block (they come in peace, apparently) and street judges have reported a large amount of frustration when dealing with crimes in the facility, mostly committed by aliens to the building (alien being anyone not from the building).

records.name: William Osler Block
records.sub: Sector 21 · William Osler Block · Owner: Dr's Medical Consortium · 100 floors
records.details:
The William Osler Block is one of the oldest medical buildings of Mega City One. Leading the way in neuroscience, the once major medicine player has become somewhat dated, with eccentric inventors and doctors all innovating medicine for the betterment of man, with no help from robots.



This is due in most part to the last will and testament of Moira MacTaggert, who left the medical business, and her fortune, to those smart enough to continue her work - with one rule: inventions should not include the aid of robots or sentient technology, in which she did not believe. Whilst some doctors have lobbied for change, others actively veto robots, citing the last will and testament of MacTaggert.



On average, the medical society of the block manage to patent a new medicine/medical practice often enough to support MacTaggert's fortune and keep the business open. In times of dire need, the Sector House has used the building as a medical facility and made reparations to the block for lost business/research.



The block is renowned for its work, however it struggles to survive in modern society, not surrendering to corporate greed. Mega Corp Campus has a far superior medical institution, but a much less reputable name.

records.name: Wombley Stadium
records.sub: Sector 21 · Wombley Stadium · Owner: FIFA · 60 floors
records.details:
Wombley Stadium recently hosted the World Cup. After extreme cases of cheating within the competition, Michelle Platt-Tiny tried to vacate the stadium with all credits generated by the event. Michelle is currently doing time in an iso-cube.



Wombley Stadium can hold approximately 100,000 citizens to watch sporting events such as the World Cup or Aeroball. There is a rumour that real grass can be found on the pitch. Facilities at the stadium have been brought into question throughout the World Cup event, with security being breached many times.

records.name: Yassin Winston
records.details:
<Redacted>

Known as "The Hammer of Sector 21," Judge Yassin Winston is one of the most feared street Judges in the sector, a towering enforcer whose presence alone can shut down a block-riot. Even by Judge standards he is heavy-handed, a blunt instrument of the Law who believes hesitation is a form of corruption. When danger erupts, Winston doesn't advance, he charges. Citizens say you can hear his boots before you see him, and by then it's already too late.

He is built like a fortress: massive frame, dark skin, dark brown hair cropped tight, a jaw carved from granite, and a stare that makes perps confess before he speaks. Winston is the kind of Judge who doesn't need intimidation techniques, his existence is one.

Winston was born in the ruins of Old Sector 5, surviving block-gang warfare before being recruited into the Academy. His instructors described him as "a natural weapon," and his psychological profile flagged him as "aggressive but controllable." The Chief Judge overrode concerns, stating: "Mega-City One needs hammers." He has served in Sector 21 for eight years, earning a reputation for ending conflicts fast, sometimes too fast. Internal Affairs has investigated him multiple times, but every inquiry ends the same way: Winston acted within the Law... technically.

Winston is blunt, disciplined, and utterly fearless. He doesn't negotiate, doesn't bargain, and doesn't tolerate excuses. His worldview is simple: "Judgment is not a debate. It's a sentence." Despite his brutality, he is not cruel. He is efficient. Above all, Winston is honorable — he would rather die than take the Law in vain. To him, his code and justice are one and the same, inseparable. He believes mercy creates repeat offenders, and repeat offenders create corpses. His stare is legendary, a cold, unblinking glare that makes even other Judges uneasy.

He respects Quinton Peal's scientific precision, tolerates Mary Glimmerfish's legal gymnastics, and distrusts Isabella Balton's temporal experiments. Winston prefers problems he can punch.

Among citizens: "If Winston shows up, run or surrender." Among Judges: "Reliable in a firefight. Terrifying everywhere else." Among criminals: "He doesn't arrest you. He ends you." Winston has single-handedly stopped a 40-man block-riot, a hover-car gang ambush, a chem-lab explosion by dragging victims out through fire, and a Skull-Hammer Heights legal-syndicate standoff (Mary Glimmerfish still hates him for it). His brutality is infamous, but his results are undeniable.
